We develop a total-Lagrangian vectorial lattice Boltzmann method that resolves this geometric mismatch for two- and three-dimensional hyperelastic dynamics. The continuum equations are written as a conservative first-order system for material velocity and deformation gradient. Vector-valued populations are chosen so that their moments recover the state and the material-coordinate Piola fluxes, giving D2Q4\(\times\)6 and D3Q6\(\times\)12 schemes from one \(D\)-dimensional construction. Curved boundaries are embedded by a level set and closed link by link through opposite-population moment identities, cut-link interpolation, and local geometric information at the boundary point. The reconstruction is coupled to a compatibility projection that keeps the recovered displacement aligned with the evolved deformation gradient on embedded active-node graphs. The resulting method extends the previous grid-aligned two-dimensional formulation to curved domains and three-dimensional lattices while retaining explicit collide-stream updates on Cartesian grids. Benchmarks in two and three dimensions show agreement with exact finite-strain fields, nonlinear radial boundary-value problems, and finite-element references.
tldr: A lattice Boltzmann method for finite-strain hyperelasticity on curved domains.
motivation: To handle curved boundaries in hyperelastic simulations using lattice Boltzmann methods, which previously were limited to grid-aligned geometries.
method: Develops a total-Lagrangian vectorial lattice Boltzmann scheme with D2Q4×6 and D3Q6×12 stencils, using level sets for boundary embedding and cut-link interpolation for missing populations.
result: The method matches exact finite-strain fields and finite-element references in 2D and 3D benchmarks.
conclusion: The approach extends lattice Boltzmann methods to curved domains for hyperelasticity while retaining explicit collide-stream updates on Cartesian grids.

title: Gauge Invariant Generalizations Of The Proca Equation And The Yang-Mills-Proca Equation
authors: Nikolay Marchuk
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20828v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Proca equations (1936) are used in quantum field theory to describe vector bosons (spin 1) with a nonzero mass. The Proca equations are not gauge invariant. In contrast to Stueckelberg's approach (1938), this article presents a gauge invariant generalization of the Proca equation by introducing an additional vector field into the Proca equation. The results are extended to the Yang-Mills-Proca equations, leading to equations with non-Abelian gauge symmetry.
tldr: This paper proposes gauge invariant generalizations of the Proca and Yang-Mills-Proca equations by introducing an additional vector field.
motivation: The Proca equation for massive vector bosons lacks gauge invariance, and the authors aim to restore it without resorting to the Stueckelberg mechanism.
method: The authors introduce an extra vector field into the Proca equation to achieve gauge invariance, then extend the construction to non-Abelian Yang-Mills-Proca equations.
result: They obtain gauge invariant equations that reduce to the original Proca and Yang-Mills-Proca equations in a specific gauge.
conclusion: The proposed generalizations provide an alternative gauge invariant formulation for massive vector fields, potentially relevant to quantum field theory.

title: Experimental Investigation Of Surface Passivation Chemistries For Optical Nanotweezers
authors: Maxwell T. Ugwu, Kewei Li, Abayomi Opadele, Theodore Anyika, Justus C. Ndukaife
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20914v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nanotweezers are actively investigated as a powerful means to reversibly trap and characterize nanoparticles with profound biological and environmental importance. To ensure that these particles can be reversibly trapped and released, surface passivation is essential. To mitigate the issue of fouling, we investigated the antifouling properties of poly(sodium styrene sulphate) (PSS) synthesized using the Atom Transfer Radical Polymerization (ATRP) technique on our previously reported gold-based Interferometric Electrohydrodynamic Tweezers (IET) device. Fluorescence and interferometric scattering (ISCAT) imaging were used to record trapping performance and study the antifouling properties of our passivated nanotweezer device. The results show that PSS exhibits superior anti-fouling performance against polystyrene nanoparticles when compared to 11-mercaptoundecanoic acid (MUA). By comparing the antifouling properties of PSS and zwitterionic poly(methacryloyloxyethyl phosphorylcholine) (PMPC) in preventing extracellular vesicle adhesion, we found that both exhibited similar performance. Overall, the ATRP technique is broadly applicable across nanotweezer substrates with appropriately chosen initiators.
tldr: This paper investigates surface passivation chemistries for optical nanotweezers to prevent fouling.
motivation: Nanotweezers are used for trapping nanoparticles, but fouling hinders reversible trapping; surface passivation is needed.
method: The authors tested poly(sodium styrene sulphate) (PSS) synthesized via ATRP on gold-based interferometric electrohydrodynamic tweezers, using fluorescence and iSCAT imaging to evaluate antifouling performance.
result: PSS showed superior antifouling against polystyrene nanoparticles compared to MUA, and similar performance to PMPC against extracellular vesicles.
conclusion: ATRP-based passivation is broadly applicable for nanotweezer substrates to reduce fouling.

title: Optical Two-Centered Charges, Dipoles, And Conveyor-Belt Modes In Bipolar Coordinates
authors: J. Strohaber
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20951v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We holographically generate optical modes associated with bipolar-coordinate solutions of the Helmholtz equation. Unlike conventional Gaussian beam families, these modes support multicenter phase discontinuities. We investigate and demonstrate that they support multicentered phase singularities, including optical dipoles and two-centered charge distributions. We further identify a family of conveyor-belt modes whose intensity structure follows an extended trajectory connecting the charge centers. Experimental generation using a spatial light modulator is presented and compared with theoretical predictions. These results establish bipolar-coordinate optical modes as a new class of structured light fields for singular optics, beam shaping, optical manipulation, and the controlled generation of multicentered topological structures.
tldr: This paper presents a new class of structured light fields based on bipolar-coordinate solutions of the Helmholtz equation, featuring multicentered phase singularities and conveyor-belt modes.
motivation: To explore and experimentally generate optical modes with multicentered phase discontinuities beyond conventional Gaussian beams, enabling new capabilities in singular optics and optical manipulation.
method: The authors theoretically derive bipolar-coordinate solutions of the Helmholtz equation, then experimentally generate the modes using a spatial light modulator and compare with theoretical predictions.
result: They demonstrate optical dipoles, two-centered charge distributions, and conveyor-belt modes whose intensity structure connects the charge centers.
conclusion: Bipolar-coordinate optical modes constitute a new class of structured light fields useful for singular optics, beam shaping, and optical manipulation.

title: Poisson Structures Of Deformed $W$-algebras And Classical $W$-algebras
authors: Uhi Rinn Suh Dong Jun Choi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21150v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we explain how classical [MATH]-algebras can be obtained as limits of [MATH]-deformed [MATH]-algebras in type [MATH]. To this end, we give a detailed examination of the construction of deformed [MATH]-algebras via Hamiltonian reduction of deformed affine Poisson algebras. We first derive an affine Poisson vertex algebra (PVA) from the Poisson structure of the deformed affine Poisson algebra. This construction identifies a specific set of generators of the deformed [MATH]-algebra with generators of the classical [MATH]-algebra.
tldr: This paper studies Poisson structures of deformed W-algebras and their relation to classical W-algebras via Hamiltonian reduction.
motivation: To understand how classical W-algebras emerge as limits of deformed W-algebras, which is a mathematical question in algebra and representation theory.
method: The authors construct deformed W-algebras via Hamiltonian reduction of deformed affine Poisson algebras and derive an affine Poisson vertex algebra from the Poisson structure.
result: They identify a specific set of generators of the deformed W-algebra with generators of the classical W-algebra.
conclusion: Classical W-algebras can be obtained as limits of deformed W-algebras in type A, providing a connection between these algebraic structures.

title: Nested Active Pointing Control For Interspacecraft Laser Interferometry
authors: Daikang Wei, Christoph Bode, Yihao Yan, Vitali M\"uller, Juan Jos\'e Esteban Delgado, Gerhard Heinzel
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Precise pointing control is a critical requirement for interspacecraft laser interferometry, as angular misalignment introduces measurement noise and even leads to laser link loss. We present a nested control architecture that uses differential wavefront sensing signals to drive a fast steering mirror (FSM) to track the incoming beam, while feeding the FSM's angular changes back to the attitude and orbit control system (AOCS) to suppress angle-dependent optical path variations. This scheme is experimentally validated in our hexapod-based setup. Relative to standalone FSM actuation, the nested configuration enhanced pointing stability by 6.9 dB and 4.9 dB in the horizontal and vertical directions across the frequency band from 3 mHz to the AOCS actuation's unity-gain frequency. Additionally, tilt-to-length coupling was suppressed by an order of magnitude below 6 mHz and by two orders of magnitude below 0.45 mHz. These results demonstrate the feasibility of nested active pointing control for future interspacecraft laser interferometry missions.
tldr: This paper presents a nested control architecture for interspacecraft laser interferometry, improving pointing stability and reducing tilt-to-length coupling.
motivation: Precise pointing control is critical for interspacecraft laser interferometry to minimize measurement noise and prevent laser link loss.
method: A nested control loop uses differential wavefront sensing to drive a fast steering mirror (FSM) for beam tracking, with FSM angular changes fed back to the attitude and orbit control system (AOCS) to suppress angle-dependent optical path variations.
result: The nested configuration enhanced pointing stability by 6.9 dB and 4.9 dB in horizontal and vertical directions (3 mHz to AOCS unity-gain frequency) and suppressed tilt-to-length coupling by one to two orders of magnitude below 6 mHz.
conclusion: The nested active pointing control scheme is feasible for future interspacecraft laser interferometry missions.

title: MADField: Multi-fidelity Amortized Density Field For Adsorption In Nanoporous Materials
authors: Yoonho Kim, Seongsu Kim, Sungsoo Ahn, Honghui Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21284v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-throughput computational screening of nanoporous materials for gas storage and separation requires fast and accurate characterization of adsorption equilibrium. Particle-based grand canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) and density-based classical density functional theory (cDFT) provide simulation-based estimates of gas uptake and adsorbate density fields, but their speed-accuracy tradeoff remains insufficient for large-scale screening. In this work, we address this gap with Multi-fidelity Amortized Density Field for Adsorption in Nanoporous Materials (MADField), which reframes adsorption prediction as equilibrium density-field estimation. MADField learns from two complementary fidelities, combining broad and scalable cDFT density supervision with higher-fidelity GCMC density labels, and recovers gas uptake by integrating the predicted density field. MADField improves uptake accuracy over the strongest baselines by 6.0x for cDFT and 15.4x for GCMC, and its predicted fields accelerate cDFT solvers with 2.0x fewer iteration steps while recovering 42 percent of cases that fail under standard settings. Finally, we evaluate MADField for conventional CH4 working capacity screening on the 270k-structure ARC-MOF database. Within this space of extremely rare high-capacity targets, 167 in total, the model achieves 56x higher average precision than the strongest baseline and accelerates inference by five orders of magnitude compared to GCMC. By prioritizing the MADField rankings, selecting the top 1.7 percent of candidates recovers 95 percent of all targets, while the top 6 percent ensures 100 percent recall.
tldr: MADField uses multi-fidelity machine learning to predict gas adsorption density fields in nanoporous materials, combining cDFT and GCMC data for faster screening.
motivation: High-throughput screening of nanoporous materials for gas storage requires fast and accurate adsorption predictions, but existing methods (GCMC, cDFT) have a speed-accuracy tradeoff.
method: The model learns from two fidelities: broad cDFT density supervision and higher-fidelity GCMC density labels, predicting equilibrium density fields and integrating them to estimate gas uptake.
result: MADField improves uptake accuracy by 6x over cDFT and 15.4x over GCMC baselines, and in CH4 screening on 270k MOFs, it achieves 56x higher average precision and 100% recall in top 6% of candidates.
conclusion: Multi-fidelity learning effectively accelerates adsorption prediction, enabling large-scale screening of nanoporous materials.

title: A Dressed Polarizability Framework For Interface-coupled Meta-atoms And Large-scale Metasurfaces
authors: Peng Fu, Jean-Paul Hugonin, Maxime Bertrand, Kevin Vynck, P. Lalanne
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21302v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The modeling of large collections of interacting meta-atoms remains a central challenge in photonics because it requires the simultaneous treatment of complex scatterer geometries, multiple scattering, and heterogeneous environments. Here, we introduce the dressed Global Polarizability Matrix (dGPM), a reduced-order electromagnetic framework in which complex meta-atoms are represented by compact scattering operators that explicitly incorporate the influence of nearby interfaces. The dGPM accurately reconstructs near- and far-field electromagnetic responses for interface-coupled structures, including geometries beyond the practical applicability of conventional T-matrix approaches. The framework naturally combines interface-coupled and free-space scatterers within a unified multiple-scattering formalism and enables simulations of large ordered and disordered metasurfaces. More broadly, the dGPM extends operator-based electromagnetic modeling to heterogeneous photonic environments while preserving a compact scatterer-based representation, providing an efficient framework for the simulation and design of large-scale photonic systems.
tldr: Introduces a dressed global polarizability matrix framework for efficient electromagnetic modeling of large metasurfaces with interface-coupled meta-atoms.
motivation: Modeling large collections of interacting meta-atoms in heterogeneous environments is computationally challenging; existing methods like T-matrix approaches are limited for interface-coupled structures.
method: The dressed Global Polarizability Matrix (dGPM) represents complex meta-atoms as compact scattering operators that incorporate interface effects, enabling unified multiple-scattering simulations.
result: The dGPM accurately reconstructs near- and far-field responses for interface-coupled structures and scales to large ordered and disordered metasurfaces.
conclusion: The framework provides an efficient, compact representation for simulating and designing large-scale photonic systems in heterogeneous environments.

title: A Delayed Generalized Lotka--Volterra Model For Threshold Instability And Structural Recognition
authors: Carlo Cattani
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20685v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a delayed generalized Lotka--Volterra model for systems in which structural change and recognition of change are not synchronized. The starting point is the idea that a system may accumulate internal transformations while remaining locally stable at the level of interpretation, governance, or perception. Instability becomes effective only when accumulated structural stress crosses a threshold and is recognized after a delay. We introduce a vector of civilizational state variables including systemic complexity, informational entropy, systemic pressure, resilience, and legitimacy. Their interaction is modeled through a delayed generalized Lotka--Volterra system. The delays represent the temporal separation between structural variation and its cognitive, institutional, or social effects. A composite instability functional is then defined, and threshold crossing is interpreted as the transition from latent instability to recognized instability. The paper studies positivity, equilibria, linearization, and local stability of the delayed system. Particular attention is given to delay-induced instability: even when the corresponding non-delayed system is locally stable, sufficiently large delays may destabilize the equilibrium and generate oscillatory or nonlinear behavior. The model provides a mathematical framework for delayed recognition, threshold instability, and the emergence of crises in complex adaptive systems.
tldr: A delayed Lotka-Volterra model for threshold instability and structural recognition in complex adaptive systems, applied to civilizational state variables.
motivation: To model systems where structural change and recognition are not synchronized, leading to delayed instability and crises.
method: Introduces a delayed generalized Lotka-Volterra system with variables like complexity, entropy, and resilience; analyzes positivity, equilibria, and delay-induced instability.
result: Shows that delays can destabilize otherwise stable equilibria, leading to oscillations or nonlinear behavior.
conclusion: Provides a mathematical framework for understanding delayed recognition and threshold instability in complex systems.

title: The Normalized Orbit Of A Bounded Normal Operator Can Be A Frame
authors: G\"otz E. Pfander Ilya A. Krishtal
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conjecture 3 in [A. Aldroubi, C. Cabrelli, I. Krishtal, and U. Molter, Dynamical Sampling: A Survey, La Matematica 5 (2026), Article 37] postulates that for any bounded normal operator [MATH] on a Hilbert space [MATH] and any vector [MATH] the system \[ \left\{{\|T^k g\|}: k=0,1,2,\ldots\right\} \] is not a frame. It was motivated by [A. Aldroubi, C. Cabrelli, A. F. akmak, U. Molter, and A. Petrosyan, Iterative actions of normal operators, J. Funct. Anal. 272 (2017), no. 3, 1121--1146], where it was established that such frames do not exist when [MATH] is a self adjoint operator. We show, however, that this conjecture is false by presenting a construction of [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH] such that the normalized orbit considered is indeed a frame. The operator is diagonal and is defined via a decomposition of the space into finite blocks rapidly increasing in size. We also provide an [MATH]-perturbation [MATH] of the operator [MATH] such that the system \[ \left\{{S^k g}: k=0,1,2,\ldots\right\} \] is a Carleson frame in the sense of [A. Aldroubi, C. Cabrelli, U. Molter, and S. Tang, Dynamical sampling, Appl. Comput. Harmon. Anal. 42 (2017), no. 3, 378--401] and [O. Christensen, M. Hasannasab, F. M. Philipp, and D. Stoeva, The mystery of Carleson frames, Appl. Comput. Harmon. Anal. 72 (2024), Article 101659]. The constructions were achieved using ChatGPT, whose assistance was also employed in the preparation of this manuscript.
tldr: This paper disproves a conjecture about frames formed by normalized orbits of bounded normal operators, constructing a counterexample using a block-diagonal operator.
motivation: The conjecture that normalized orbits of bounded normal operators cannot form frames was motivated by prior work on self-adjoint operators; the authors aim to show it is false.
method: The authors construct a diagonal operator on a Hilbert space decomposed into finite blocks of rapidly increasing size, and define a vector such that the normalized orbit forms a frame.
result: They provide an explicit counterexample to Conjecture 3, and also construct a perturbation that yields a Carleson frame.
conclusion: The conjecture is false; normalized orbits of bounded normal operators can indeed be frames, contrary to previous expectations.

title: Neural Network Approximation In Discrete Dual Norms With Adaptive Test Spaces
authors: Tanakorn Udomworarat, Ignacio Brevis, Kristoffer G. van der Zee, Sergio Rojas
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In robust variational physics-informed neural networks (RVPINNs), the loss function is formulated in terms of the Riesz representative of the variational residual within a discrete test space. This approach guarantees that the loss function is robust with respect to the true error in the energy norm up to a remainder term that depends on both the neural network approximation and the discrete space configuration. However, in problems with localized singularities, steep gradients, or interface layers, a fixed coarse test space may fail to resolve the continuous Riesz representative of the residual during training. Although this can be avoided by using a sufficiently fine test space from the start, doing so may be computationally inefficient. We therefore propose an adaptive algorithm that enriches the test space only where the error between the discrete and continuous Riesz representatives is pronounced. We establish theoretical adaptive strategies within the RVPINN framework and derive their error bounds. Furthermore, we propose a computable refinement indicator and prove that, under the saturation assumption, it serves as a reliable and efficient error estimator for the non-computable discrepancy between the discrete and continuous Riesz representatives. Finally, we propose a practical adaptive algorithm and demonstrate its effectiveness through numerical experiments on elliptic Dirichlet problems.
tldr: This paper proposes an adaptive algorithm for enriching test spaces in robust variational physics-informed neural networks (RVPINNs) to improve approximation in problems with localized features.
motivation: Fixed coarse test spaces in RVPINNs may fail to resolve the continuous Riesz representative of the residual in problems with singularities or steep gradients, while using a fine test space from the start is computationally inefficient.
method: The authors develop an adaptive algorithm that enriches the test space where the error between discrete and continuous Riesz representatives is large, using a computable refinement indicator based on the saturation assumption.
result: The refinement indicator is proven to be a reliable and efficient error estimator for the discrepancy between discrete and continuous Riesz representatives, and numerical experiments on elliptic Dirichlet problems demonstrate the effectiveness of the adaptive algorithm.
conclusion: The adaptive test space enrichment improves the efficiency and accuracy of RVPINNs for problems with localized features, without requiring a uniformly fine test space.

title: On The Weight Spectrum Of The Reed-Muller Codes $rm(7,14)$
authors: Manuel Albrizzio Milo Leuenberger
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we attempt to find the weight spectrum of the Reed-Muller codes [MATH]. In the process, we tried to fully determine the weight spectrum of [MATH]. We found almost all of the weights, except for a select number of them. The remaining eight missing weights are necessary to give a positive answer to an open question on the weight spectrum of [MATH] for [MATH].
tldr: This paper attempts to determine the weight spectrum of Reed-Muller codes RM(7,14), finding almost all weights except eight missing ones.
motivation: The weight spectrum of Reed-Muller codes is a classical problem in coding theory, and completing it for RM(7,14) answers an open question.
method: The authors use combinatorial and algebraic techniques to compute the weight distribution of the code.
result: They found almost all weights of RM(7,14), with eight weights remaining unknown.
conclusion: The work contributes to the classification of weight spectra for Reed-Muller codes, but the missing weights leave the problem partially open.

title: Non-commutative Calculus And Getzler-Gauss-Manin Connections For Open-closed Homotopy Algebras
authors: Zekai Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the calculus structure on Hochschild invariants of open-closed homotopy algebras. We further define the Getzler-Gauss-Manin connection and show that it is flat up to chain homotopy on the open-closed periodic cyclic chain complex.
tldr: The paper develops a non-commutative calculus and Getzler-Gauss-Manin connection for open-closed homotopy algebras, focusing on algebraic structures in homotopy theory.
motivation: To extend the calculus structure and Gauss-Manin connection to the setting of open-closed homotopy algebras, which are important in algebraic topology and mathematical physics.
method: The author establishes a calculus structure on Hochschild invariants and defines a Getzler-Gauss-Manin connection on the open-closed periodic cyclic chain complex, proving flatness up to chain homotopy.
result: A flat Getzler-Gauss-Manin connection is constructed for open-closed homotopy algebras, generalizing known results in cyclic homology.
conclusion: This work provides a foundational algebraic framework that may have applications in string topology and deformation theory, but is not directly connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Tutorial On Bregman Projection In Statistics
authors: Gunhee Cho, Jae Kwang Kim, Yumou Qiu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A single geometric operation -- projecting a reference onto a constrained family under a Bregman divergence -- underlies a striking range of statistical methods. This tutorial develops the operation first as pure convex geometry, with no statistics attached. A strictly convex generator [MATH] and its conjugate [MATH] furnish two coordinate systems, a projection theorem with existence and uniqueness, and a Pythagorean {theorem}; the Pythagorean theorem itself produces {two} dual projections -- the information (e-) projection onto moment-constrained families and the moment (m-) projection onto exponential families -- exchanged by the conjugacy [MATH], so a single theorem governs both. Part~II reads off the statistics. The generalized linear model is treated in detail as the concrete carrier of the two projections: {under the canonical link,} the score equation is exactly the Pythagorean orthogonality, and the fit is simultaneously an e-projection in the natural coordinate and an m-projection in the mean coordinate. Maximum entropy, survey calibration, over-identified moment models, the EM algorithm, variational inference, autoencoders, and expectation propagation then fall into place as instances of the same construction -- exactly where the underlying families are flat, and as controlled approximations or neighboring-divergence analogies where they are not. The mathematics of Part~I is self-contained; the statistical sections presume only familiarity with the methods being unified.
tldr: A tutorial on Bregman projection unifying various statistical methods through convex geometry.
motivation: To show that many statistical algorithms (GLM, EM, variational inference) are instances of a single geometric operation: Bregman projection.
method: Develops Bregman divergence and projection theorems in convex analysis, then applies them to statistical models.
result: Demonstrates that score equations, maximum entropy, and other methods correspond to e- and m-projections under Bregman divergence.
conclusion: Bregman projection provides a unifying geometric framework for a wide range of statistical techniques.

title: Privacy-Preserving Compliance On Public Ledgers Via Selective Disclosure Authorization Schemes
authors: Sanchari Das Supriya Khadka
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20760v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Public distributed ledgers enforce integrity through radical transparency, creating tension with data minimization principles required for regulatory compliance. While Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs) offer a theoretical privacy solution, existing constructions often overlook adversarial constraints in smart contract environments. Specifically, the asynchronous decoupling of off-chain proof generation from on-chain submission introduces front-running and proof-reuse risks in public mempools. In this work, we formalize Selective Disclosure Authorization Schemes (SDAS), a cryptographic primitive for granular and revocable compliance checks on public ledgers without revealing the underlying witness. We define a security model for SDAS, introducing Ledger-Bound Attribute Unlinkability and Context-Aware Sender Binding to capture how valid proofs remain bound to their intended authorization context. To validate sender binding, we present ZK-Compliance, an Ethereum-based instantiation that operationalizes a user-controlled "Grant, Verify, Revoke" lifecycle. We implement the sender-binding component using a 14-constraint Circom circuit that anchors the zero-knowledge proof to the executing on-chain sender address. Our Sepolia evaluation confirms practical viability: browser-based proof generation executes in under 200 ms, and on-chain verification costs 240,512 gas, neutralizing proof reuse by different callers while preserving strict attribute privacy.
tldr: This paper introduces Selective Disclosure Authorization Schemes (SDAS) for privacy-preserving compliance on public ledgers using zero-knowledge proofs, with an Ethereum implementation.
motivation: Public ledgers enforce transparency but conflict with data minimization for regulatory compliance; existing ZKP solutions overlook adversarial risks in smart contract environments like front-running and proof-reuse.
method: The authors formalize SDAS with security models (Ledger-Bound Attribute Unlinkability, Context-Aware Sender Binding) and implement ZK-Compliance on Ethereum using a 14-constraint Circom circuit to anchor proofs to sender addresses.
result: Browser-based proof generation takes under 200 ms, on-chain verification costs 240,512 gas, and the scheme neutralizes proof reuse while preserving attribute privacy.
conclusion: SDAS provides a practical cryptographic primitive for granular, revocable compliance on public ledgers, demonstrated via a viable Ethereum instantiation.

title: PromptMark: A Prompt-Guided Iterative-Feedback Framework For Source Code Watermarking
authors: Istiaq Ahmed Fahad, Mridha Md. Nafis Fuad, Kazi Sakib
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20835v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Watermarking has become a crucial technique for ensuring provenance and accountability in AI-generated source code. As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into development workflows, reliable attribution remains challenging. In practice, most developers rely on commercial LLM APIs operating under black-box constraints, making existing approaches that require access to the decoding process less feasible for real-world integration. To address this limitation, we propose PromptMark, a black-box, prompt-guided watermarking framework that embeds invisible yet statistically detectable signals into generated code via structured input instructions. The method steers models toward subtle identifier and comment naming patterns while preserving the functional correctness and structural integrity of the generated code. Detection is performed using statistical tests designed to remain reliable across varying code lengths and model outputs. The embedding is further refined through an iterative feedback loop, where prompts are updated based on watermark detection scores. Experiments on the MBPP and HumanEval benchmarks show that PromptMark consistently achieves strong watermark detectability while maintaining high code correctness, outperforming baseline approaches.
tldr: A black-box watermarking framework for AI-generated source code using prompt-guided iterative feedback.
motivation: Existing watermarking methods require access to the LLM decoding process, which is not feasible with commercial black-box APIs.
method: PromptMark embeds invisible signals into generated code via structured prompts that steer identifier and comment naming patterns, refined through an iterative feedback loop based on detection scores.
result: Experiments on MBPP and HumanEval show strong watermark detectability while maintaining high code correctness, outperforming baselines.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical solution for provenance and accountability in AI-generated code under black-box constraints.

title: A Blockchain Consensus Mechanism For Distributed Electricity Trading
authors: Shanglin Yang, Guo Chen, Shiping Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21060v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distributed power systems complement centralized grids by coordinating distributed energy resources (DERs) to achieve regional energy self-sufficiency. Scaling such systems raises four persistent challenges: decentralized coordination, fair economic settlement, trustworthy operation, and system optimization, all without a central authority. This paper proposes Proof of Energy (PoE), a blockchain consensus mechanism that addresses these challenges through cryptographically secured, contribution-proportional node selection. In PoE, block generation rights are tied directly to real-world energy contributions, enabling distributed consensus without centralized dispatch. An Energy Contribution Unit (ECU) model is introduced to map heterogeneous energy services onto a unified value metric via scarcity-weighted normalization. A Verifiable Random Function (VRF)-based proposal mechanism then ensures selection probability is strictly proportional to node contribution, preserving fairness and resisting manipulation. Case studies validate PoE across three dimensions: grid coordination, incentive fairness, and optimization efficiency. The result is a cryptographically secured, incentive-compatible framework for decentralized value distribution in energy systems.
tldr: This paper proposes a blockchain consensus mechanism for distributed electricity trading, using energy contributions to determine block generation rights.
motivation: Distributed power systems face challenges in decentralized coordination, fair settlement, and trustworthy operation without a central authority.
method: The authors introduce Proof of Energy (PoE), which ties block generation rights to real-world energy contributions via an Energy Contribution Unit (ECU) model and Verifiable Random Function (VRF)-based selection.
result: Case studies validate PoE across grid coordination, incentive fairness, and optimization efficiency.
conclusion: PoE provides a cryptographically secured, incentive-compatible framework for decentralized value distribution in energy systems.

title: Verification Of Parametric Markov Automata Under Time-bounded Reachability
authors: Kevin van de Glind, Matthias Volk, Tim Willemse
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21444v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Analysis of Markov models is of high importance for formal verification. Until now, analysis of Markov Automata required them to be fully specified, which is a considerable restriction as rates may be unknown or influenced by uncertainty of the environment. We introduce parametric Markov Automata (pMA) to capture this uncertainty with parametric transition functions. On these parametrized models, two different synthesis problems for time-bounded reachability properties are considered: I) Does there exist a valuation in the parameter space such that the instantiated model satisfies/violates the property, and II) given the parameter space, how can it be partitioned into satisfying and violating regions? Our approach comprises two steps: I) The pMA is discretized to a parametric Markov decision process (pMDP), and II) through analysis of the pMDP, bounds are obtained for the reachability probability in the parametric MA. This approach solves the above problems up to a specified precision, as the accumulated error terms can be made arbitrarily small. We implemented the approach using the Storm model checker. Our experimental evaluation shows that the main performance bottlenecks originate from the discretization of the pMA.
tldr: This paper introduces parametric Markov automata for verification of time-bounded reachability properties under parameter uncertainty.
motivation: Traditional Markov automata analysis requires fully specified models, which is restrictive when rates are unknown or uncertain. The authors aim to handle this uncertainty by introducing parameters.
method: They discretize parametric Markov automata into parametric Markov decision processes and analyze them to obtain bounds on reachability probabilities with controlled error.
result: The approach solves two synthesis problems: existence of a valuation satisfying/violating a property, and partitioning the parameter space into satisfying and violating regions, with arbitrarily small error.
conclusion: The method is implemented in the Storm model checker and shows that discretization is the main performance bottleneck.

title: Mobility-Informed Coupling Of Abm, Pde, And Ode Models For Pandemic Simulation In Germany
authors: Tim O. F. Conrad Kristina Kehrer
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20652v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a hybrid modeling framework for simulating the spread of COVID-19 across Germany. Our approach couples high-resolution agent-based models (ABMs) incorporating mobility data from mobile phones with faster, less detailed partial differential equation (PDE) and ordinary differential equation (ODE) models. Mobility between regions is incorporated through data-driven jump processes that transfer individuals, enabling a balance between accuracy and computational efficiency. Building on earlier studies on pairwise ABM-ODE, ABM-PDE, and PDE-ODE coupling strategies, we develop a hybrid model to unify all three model classes (ABM, PDE, and ODE) within a single framework. To demonstrate the framework's utility, we systematically compare ABM, PDE, and ODE representations of Berlin embedded in a nationwide simulation of Germany, investigating complete travel restrictions to and from selected federal states, and evaluating the Zero-COVID and No-COVID strategies. These experiments demonstrate how the framework can be used to analyze the interplay between mobility, regional coupling, and containment measures at the scale of an entire country. Computational performance is analyzed by measuring runtime savings while quantifying error using real-world infection data. The presented framework enables efficient and accurate simulation of infection dynamics across densely connected regions and provides a tool for evidence-based evaluation of public health interventions.
tldr: A hybrid modeling framework coupling ABM, PDE, and ODE models for pandemic simulation in Germany.
motivation: To balance accuracy and computational efficiency in simulating COVID-19 spread across Germany using mobility data.
method: Couples high-resolution agent-based models with PDE and ODE models via data-driven jump processes for inter-regional mobility.
result: Demonstrates the framework on scenarios like travel restrictions and Zero-COVID strategies, analyzing runtime savings and error against real data.
conclusion: The framework enables efficient and accurate simulation of infection dynamics for evidence-based public health interventions.

title: A Benchmark Generator Of Realistic Logistic Transport Networks With Nonlinear Edge Costs And Transshipment Capacities
authors: Alexander Ponomarenko Varvara Kovaleva
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Routing many commodities through a logistic network at minimum joint cost of vehicle movements and transshipment at intermediate storages becomes substantially harder -- and substantially more realistic -- once two features are present together: edge costs that are in the transported volume, because freight travels in fixed-capacity vehicles, and on the volume reloaded at each storage. No public benchmark captures this combination, and the locations of commercial distribution centres are proprietary. We close this gap with a parameterised generator of synthetic logistic networks, calibrated on real road graphs of nine European countries, five U.S.\ states and the European part of Russia extracted from OpenStreetMap. The generator reproduces the structural signatures of upper-level distribution networks -- near-planar topology, low vertex degree, short edges and large diameters -- by combining Zipf-distributed city sizes, a spatial-network budget model trading edge-building cost against routing convenience, centrality-driven storage capacities, and a doubly constrained gravity demand model. We release 35 fully synthetic instances ([MATH]--[MATH] storages) and 15 real-geometry instances in an open, self-describing, fully reproducible file format. An empirical characterisation computed directly from the released files shows that synthetic and real-geometry instances are structurally consistent (two-sample Kolmogorov--Smirnov distances of [MATH] on degree and edge-length distributions, with small and quantified mean deviations), and a baseline-solver study demonstrates that the corpus discriminates instance difficulty across orders of magnitude. The benchmark is a faithful, reusable testbed for the development and comparison of exact and heuristic algorithms.
tldr: This paper presents a benchmark generator for logistic transport networks with nonlinear edge costs and transshipment capacities, calibrated on real road data.
motivation: No public benchmark captures the combination of nonlinear edge costs and transshipment capacities in logistic networks, and commercial distribution center locations are proprietary.
method: The generator combines Zipf-distributed city sizes, a spatial-network budget model, centrality-driven storage capacities, and a doubly constrained gravity demand model, calibrated on OpenStreetMap data from multiple regions.
result: 35 fully synthetic and 15 real-geometry instances are released, structurally consistent with real networks, and a baseline solver study shows the corpus discriminates instance difficulty across orders of magnitude.
conclusion: The benchmark provides a faithful, reusable testbed for developing and comparing exact and heuristic algorithms for logistic network routing.

title: The Sustainability Paradox Of Biodegradable Packaging: A Life Cycle Perspective On Chitosan-Based Food Packaging
authors: Maria Cosic, Milena Cosic, Amy Kim, Siddhartha Pahari, Grace Wu, Rayna Zhou, Trisha Daftari, Shaily Gupta, Reyna Michelle Suneel, Srinivasan Latha, Rashi Sharma, Utkarsh Chadha
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chitosan-based nanomaterials are being increasingly explored as sustainable alternatives to petroleum-derived food packaging, yet their environmental performance across the full life cycle remains insufficiently understood. This review critically evaluates these systems from a life cycle perspective and examines how material origin, processing pathways, functional performance, and end-of-life behavior collectively influence sustainability outcomes. Beginning with chitin extraction from crustacean waste, key processing steps, including demineralization, deproteinization, and nanoparticle synthesis, are assessed in terms of chemical intensity, energy demand, and associated emissions. Manufacturing routes, including solvent-based and green synthesis approaches, are compared with those of conventional plastics to identify relative environmental burdens. The use phase is analyzed with respect to antimicrobial functionality, shelf life extension, and potential reductions in food waste. End-of-life pathways, including biodegradation and composting, are evaluated alongside uncertainties related to degradation behavior and nanoparticle fate. By synthesizing these stagewise interactions, this review highlights critical trade-offs that are often overlooked in sustainability narratives and examines whether chitosan-based nanomaterials provide net environmental benefits in food packaging applications.
tldr: This paper reviews the environmental sustainability of chitosan-based biodegradable food packaging from a life cycle perspective.
motivation: Chitosan-based nanomaterials are proposed as sustainable alternatives to petroleum-based packaging, but their full environmental impact is not well understood.
method: The authors critically evaluate the life cycle stages including chitin extraction, processing, manufacturing, use phase, and end-of-life, comparing with conventional plastics.
result: The review identifies trade-offs such as chemical intensity and energy demand in processing versus biodegradability and food waste reduction benefits.
conclusion: Chitosan-based packaging may not provide net environmental benefits unless processing impacts are minimized and end-of-life behavior is better understood.

title: Mechanism Underlying The Scaling Law Of Home-return Probability In Human Mobility
authors: Xiao-Yong Yan Haoying Niu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Individual daily mobility exhibits a striking scaling law: the probability of returning home after a tour of [MATH] locations decays as [MATH]. While the tour-terminate-continue (TTC) model reproduces this behavior, it relies on this power law as an empirical input, leaving the microscopic origin of [MATH] unresolved. Here we show that this scaling emerges from a utility trade-off governed by cognitive constraints. By invoking the principle of least effort, we demonstrate that individual activity priorities follow Zipf's law, [MATH], which directly dictates the sublinear accumulation of tour utility, [MATH]. Luce's choice rule then yields [MATH], giving the exact exponent [MATH]. Agent-based simulations confirm this analytical relation. Our framework bridges the gap between individual cognitive constraints and the scaling law of tour behavior, providing a microscopic theoretical underpinning for human mobility.
tldr: This paper explains the scaling law of home-return probability in human mobility using cognitive constraints and Zipf's law.
motivation: The scaling law of home-return probability was previously reproduced by a model that relied on the power law as an empirical input, leaving its microscopic origin unresolved.
method: The authors invoke the principle of least effort to derive Zipf's law for activity priorities, then use Luce's choice rule to obtain the exact exponent of the scaling law.
result: They show that individual activity priorities follow Zipf's law, leading to sublinear accumulation of tour utility and the exact exponent -1 for the home-return probability.
conclusion: The framework bridges cognitive constraints and the scaling law, providing a microscopic theoretical underpinning for human mobility.

title: Multifunctional Imaging With An Inverse-Designed Nonlocal Metasurface
authors: Lincoln Clark, Yang Xu, Cat-Uyen Phan, David J. Byrne, Shikun Ma, Lukas Wesemann, Elizabeth Hinde, Kylie L. Gorringe, Ann Roberts
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21051v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonlocal metasurfaces enable all-optical processing of spatial information in optical fields. Here, we demonstrate a topology-optimised metasurface that switches between phase-contrast and brightfield imaging modalities via polarisation control, eliminating the need to reposition optical components or use computational techniques to image transparent samples. Specifically, for one polarisation state, an asymmetric transfer function about normal incidence performs a first order derivative on the phase, producing pseudo-3D phase-contrast images of transparent biological samples while the orthogonal state returns the result of the identity operator. This work extends inverse-design methods to reconfigurable phase-contrast microscopy and quantitative analogue optical computation with applications in biological imaging, medical diagnostics, and materials characterisation.
tldr: This paper presents a topology-optimized nonlocal metasurface that switches between phase-contrast and brightfield imaging via polarization control.
motivation: To achieve reconfigurable phase-contrast microscopy without moving parts or computational post-processing, enabling label-free imaging of transparent biological samples.
method: Inverse design (topology optimization) of a nonlocal metasurface that implements a first-order derivative operator for one polarization and identity for the orthogonal polarization.
result: The metasurface produces pseudo-3D phase-contrast images for one polarization and brightfield images for the other, demonstrated on transparent biological samples.
conclusion: This work extends inverse-design methods to reconfigurable phase-contrast microscopy and quantitative analog optical computation, with applications in biological imaging and diagnostics.

title: Boundary-conformal Integration For The Invariant-imbedding T-matrix Method: High-order Convergence For Faceted Particles
authors: Yu Xiong Zihua Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21063v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The invariant-imbedding T-matrix method (IITM) is a standard tool for light scattering by large, sharply faceted, non-axisymmetric particles (atmospheric ice crystals and mineral dust) where the surface-based extended boundary condition method loses accuracy. Its accuracy is limited by "staircasing": the dielectric contrast of a faceted particle is integrated across boundaries that cut the quadrature grid, so standard quadrature converges at low algebraic order. We show that this non-smoothness has a single geometric origin, the tangencies of the integration sphere to the faces and edges of the particle, which produce jumps, kinks, and half-integer branches according to the tangency type, in all three integration directions. A boundary-conformal scheme removes them using closed-form azimuthal coefficients, panel splitting at the analytically known tangency loci, and a square-root substitution [MATH] that absorbs the half-integer branches. For a hexagonal prism the azimuthal integration becomes exact and the zenithal and radial directions recover spectral and fourth-order convergence; because the construction depends only on the contact geometry, it extends to any convex polyhedron, demonstrated on the solid hexagonal bullet (a faceted ice habit with tilted faces). The zenithal crossing is a square-root branch rather than a kink, so the established interval-splitting alone gives only [MATH], while the radial step removes the half-integer edge branch that caps the Riccati recurrence on faceted particles. The convergence orders are fixed by the local contact geometry and verified size-independent up to [MATH]; what grows with size is the resolution needed to reach each asymptotic regime, not the order.
tldr: This paper improves the numerical convergence of the invariant-imbedding T-matrix method for light scattering by faceted particles using boundary-conformal integration.
motivation: The invariant-imbedding T-matrix method suffers from low-order convergence due to staircasing when applied to faceted particles like ice crystals.
method: The authors identify the geometric origin of the non-smoothness and develop a boundary-conformal scheme with closed-form azimuthal coefficients, panel splitting, and a square-root substitution to remove singularities.
result: The scheme achieves exact azimuthal integration and spectral or fourth-order convergence in other directions, verified for hexagonal prisms and bullets.
conclusion: The method extends to any convex polyhedron and improves accuracy for light scattering simulations of atmospheric particles.

title: Mid-infrared-to-ultraviolet Supercontinuum Generation In Low-loss Tantalum Pentoxide Nanophotonic Waveguides
authors: Minghui Li, Qiankun Li, Xhizhi Zheng, Xueying Sun, Renhong Gao, Fan Jiang, Hairun Guo, Jintian Lin, Ya Cheng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21118v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical frequency combs on photonic integrated platforms are revolutionizing precision metrology, bio-imaging, atomic and molecular sensing, and ultrafast photonics, yet most remain confined to the near-infrared. This restriction prevents access to the ultraviolet, visible, and mid-infrared bands critical for a vast array of quantum, atomic, and molecular systems. The fundamental obstacle has been the lack of a nanophotonic waveguide that simultaneously provides an ultra-broad transparency window, engineered dispersion, ultra-low propagation loss, and a strong Kerr nonlinearity, all while suppressing detrimental two-photon absorption at short wavelengths. Here, we overcome this challenge by exploring tantalum pentoxide for ultra-broadband supercontinuum spanning continuously from the ultraviolet to the mid-infrared, leveraging its broad transparency window (300-8000 nm), a high nonlinear refractive index three times larger than that of silicon nitride, and a wide bandgap that suppresses two-photon absorption. Critically, by using a photolithography assisted chemo-mechanical etching process that avoids a lossy SiO2 upper cladding, we achieve dispersion engineered waveguides with record-low propagation losses of 0.066 dB/cm at telecom wavelengths and 0.43 dB/cm at 780 nm, significantly facilitating the supercontinuum spectral extension into the ultraviolet and the mid-infrared. Pumping these anomalous-dispersion waveguides with femtosecond pulses at 1550 nm yields a gap-free, 3.2-octave supercontinuum spanning from 350 to 3200 nm via a soliton-based dynamics at only 54 pJ pulse energy, representing the broadest comb spectrum on this platform. We further demonstrate a relatively flat spectrum with a -30 dB bandwidth of 1182 nm by engineering normal dispersion, validate the comb coherence via heterodyne detection, and achieve soliton-effect pulse self-compression from 126.7 fs to 19.2 fs.
tldr: Demonstrates ultra-broadband supercontinuum generation from mid-infrared to ultraviolet in tantalum pentoxide nanophotonic waveguides.
motivation: Existing photonic integrated frequency combs are mostly confined to near-infrared, limiting access to ultraviolet, visible, and mid-infrared bands needed for quantum, atomic, and molecular systems.
method: Fabricated dispersion-engineered tantalum pentoxide waveguides using photolithography-assisted chemo-mechanical etching to achieve low loss and strong Kerr nonlinearity, then pumped with femtosecond pulses at 1550 nm.
result: Achieved a 3.2-octave supercontinuum spanning 350–3200 nm with record-low propagation losses (0.066 dB/cm at telecom, 0.43 dB/cm at 780 nm) and soliton self-compression from 126.7 fs to 19.2 fs.
conclusion: Tantalum pentoxide is a promising platform for ultra-broadband integrated photonics, enabling frequency combs that cover ultraviolet to mid-infrared for applications in sensing, metrology, and quantum optics.

title: Non-line-of-sight Imaging With Arbitrary Relay Surface Geometries Via 3d Gaussian Transient Rendering
authors: Yi Wang, Ziyu Zhan, Yuran Wang, Hao Wang, Qiang Liu, Zuoqiang Shi, Lingyun Qiu, Xing Fu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21270v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Imaging objects hidden outside the direct line of sight expands the effective field of view and is critical for applications such as autonomous driving and robotic perception. Despite impressive progress in time-of-flight (ToF)-based non-line-of-sight (NLOS) imaging, real-world deployment remains challenging because practical measurements are often collected over spatially limited, arbitrarily shaped relay regions-conditions that violate the planar-wall and dense-sampling assumptions made by most existing methods. To address these limitations, we propose a LOS-guided NLOS imaging pipeline that imposes no geometric assumptions on the relay surface and naturally supports both confocal and non-confocal configurations. Our method represents the hidden scene using 3D Gaussian primitives and couples them with an efficient, differentiable transient rendering model, enabling end-to-end optimization directly from measured transients. We validate our approach on real-world measurements from both a public dataset and a custom-built capture system. Across settings, our method achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction fidelity under spatially limited, sparsely sampled conditions, and significantly outperforms existing methods on complex, arbitrary relay surface geometries.
tldr: This paper presents a non-line-of-sight imaging method using 3D Gaussian primitives and differentiable transient rendering, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Existing NLOS imaging methods assume planar relay surfaces and dense sampling, limiting real-world deployment. The authors aim to handle arbitrary relay geometries and sparse measurements.
method: The hidden scene is represented as 3D Gaussian primitives, and a differentiable transient rendering model is used to optimize the scene representation directly from measured time-of-flight data.
result: The method achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction fidelity on real-world data with spatially limited, sparsely sampled measurements and complex relay surface geometries.
conclusion: The proposed pipeline removes geometric assumptions on the relay surface and supports both confocal and non-confocal configurations, advancing practical NLOS imaging.

title: Direct Evidence For Projectile Electronic Structure Effects In Slow Multielectron Capture Collisions
authors: Akash Srivastav, Sumit Srivastav, Bhas Bapat
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21285v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the role of the electronic structure of the projectile in ionization and subsequent fragmentation of CO[MATH] induced by multielectron capture in collisions at 0.31 a.u. impact velocity. Focusing on the [MATH] break-up channel as a representative channel, we report kinetic energy release distributions (KERDs) for collisions with equi-velocity N[MATH] and O[MATH] projectiles. We consider two complementary categories of measurements. In the first category, in which different projectiles of the same charge are considered, we find that KERDs obtained with N[MATH] and O[MATH] impact ([MATH]) are broadly similar, but they differ significantly from the earlier reported KERD with Ar[MATH] impact. In the second category, pronounced differences are observed between the KERDs obtained with isoelectronic N[MATH] and O[MATH] ([MATH]) projectiles. These results provide direct evidence that projectile electronic structure plays a critical role in multielectron capture collisions.
tldr: This paper studies projectile electronic structure effects in slow multielectron capture collisions using kinetic energy release distributions.
motivation: To understand the role of projectile electronic structure in ionization and fragmentation of molecules during ion collisions.
method: Experimental measurements of kinetic energy release distributions for CO2 break-up induced by N2+ and O2+ projectiles at 0.31 a.u. impact velocity.
result: KERDs differ significantly between Ar2+ and N2+/O2+ projectiles, and also between isoelectronic N2+ and O2+ projectiles.
conclusion: Projectile electronic structure critically influences multielectron capture collisions.

title: Dynamic Dark-field Ffoct And Dynamic Reflection Differential Phase Contrast For Label-free Functional Imaging At Reflective Biomaterial Interfaces
authors: Tual Monfort
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21314v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strong reflections from metallic and engineered substrates severely limit label-free functional imaging of living cells at biomaterial interfaces, neural electrodes, and implantable devices. Here we introduce two complementary approaches for recovering intracellular dynamic contrast at highly reflective interfaces. Dynamic dark-field full-field optical coherence tomography (D-dFFOCT) suppresses the dominant substrate reflection and restores intracellular visibility through selective detection of scattered light. In parallel, asymmetric illumination generates a distinct directional dynamic contrast that is most consistently interpreted as dynamic reflection differential phase contrast (D-RDPC). Both approaches reveal intracellular activity that remains poorly visible with conventional dynamic full-field optical coherence tomography. D-RDPC exhibits characteristic signatures of phase-gradient imaging, including contrast reversal upon illumination inversion, enhancement with increasing illumination asymmetry, and recovery of spatial localization through directional Hilbert-transform reconstruction. Together, these results establish new strategies for functional imaging at reflective interfaces and suggest that differential phase contrast signals can support temporal fluctuation analysis.
tags: dynamic dark-field full-field optical coherence tomography
tldr: This paper introduces two label-free optical imaging techniques for recovering intracellular dynamic contrast at highly reflective biomaterial interfaces.
motivation: Strong reflections from metallic and engineered substrates severely limit label-free functional imaging of living cells at biomaterial interfaces, neural electrodes, and implantable devices.
method: Dynamic dark-field full-field optical coherence tomography (D-dFFOCT) suppresses substrate reflection by selective detection of scattered light, and dynamic reflection differential phase contrast (D-RDPC) uses asymmetric illumination to generate directional dynamic contrast.
result: Both approaches reveal intracellular activity that is poorly visible with conventional dynamic full-field optical coherence tomography, with D-RDPC showing characteristic phase-gradient imaging signatures.
conclusion: These methods establish new strategies for functional imaging at reflective interfaces and suggest that differential phase contrast signals can support temporal fluctuation analysis.
keywords: dynamic dark-field full-field optical coherence tomography

title: Error Analysis For A Nonconforming Finite Element Discretization Of The 3d-ccpf Model
authors: Cl\'ement Adand\'e, Koffi W. Hou\'edanou, Guy A. D\`egla
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20665v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents an a-priori and a-posteriori error analysis for the time-dependent case of a coupled continuum pipe-fow in three dimensions on anisotropic meshes (i.e. elements with very large aspect ratio). Our investigation includes nonconforming discretizations as well as different elements and different versions of Crouzeix-Raviart fnite element methods. Under suitable regularity assumptions on the exact solution, we derive optimal a priori error estimates in the H^1-like norm. Leveraging residual elements, local error indicators and a global estimator are generated, demonstrating reliability and efficiency. The efficiency of error estimators holds unconditional, though its reliability involves the alignment measure notion. Mesh requirements are established to ensure the optimality of the error estimator.
tldr: This paper presents error analysis for a nonconforming finite element discretization of a 3D coupled continuum pipe flow model.
motivation: To develop and analyze numerical methods for simulating coupled pipe flow in three dimensions, which is important for engineering applications.
method: The authors use nonconforming finite element methods (Crouzeix-Raviart) on anisotropic meshes and derive a priori and a posteriori error estimates using residual-based error indicators.
result: Optimal a priori error estimates in H^1-like norm are derived, and reliable and efficient error estimators are constructed, with efficiency unconditional and reliability involving an alignment measure.
conclusion: The proposed error estimators are effective for adaptive mesh refinement, and mesh requirements ensure optimality.

title: Optimal Play, Nontransitivity, And Nash Equilibria In Dice Bingo
authors: Benjamin W. Ong David J. Hemmer
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Dice Bingo, a game in which players fill a [MATH] bingo board whose entries are possible sums of two fair dice. After each roll, a player marks one matching square, and the goal is to complete a row, column, or diagonal. We model optimal play for a fixed board as a finite Markov decision process and derive Bellman equations that compute the exact expected number of rolls required to obtain a bingo. Using this framework, we identify a unique optimal board up to natural symmetries and determine its exact expected completion time. We then investigate head-to-head competition in which two players observe the same sequence of dice rolls. By analyzing a joint Markov chain that tracks both boards simultaneously, we compute (in exact arithmetic) win, loss, and tie probabilities. Surprisingly, a board with a worse expected completion time can nevertheless be favored in head-to-head competition. Motivated by this phenomenon, we exhibit nontransitive triples of bingo boards: board [MATH] is favored against board [MATH], board [MATH] is favored against board [MATH], and board [MATH] is favored against board [MATH]. Finally, we consider strategic play in which players adapt their choices to their opponent's board rather than merely minimizing their own completion time. In this setting, optimal decisions depend on the opponent's state, leading naturally to game-theoretic analysis. We present a position with no pure Nash equilibrium and compute an explicit mixed Nash equilibrium.
tldr: This paper analyzes optimal play and game-theoretic equilibria in a dice-based bingo game, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The authors aim to model optimal strategies and discover nontransitive preferences in a stochastic game, motivated by the surprising phenomenon that a board with worse expected completion time can be favored in head-to-head play.
method: They formulate optimal play as a finite Markov decision process and derive Bellman equations for expected completion time. Head-to-head competition is analyzed via a joint Markov chain, and strategic play is studied using game theory to find Nash equilibria.
result: They identify a unique optimal board up to symmetries, compute exact expected completion times, and exhibit nontransitive triples of boards. They also find positions with no pure Nash equilibrium and compute mixed Nash equilibria.
conclusion: The work provides a complete game-theoretic analysis of Dice Bingo, revealing nontransitivity and strategic complexity, but it is entirely unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Lectures Notes On Number Theory For Computer Science
authors: Alexandros V. Gerbessiotis
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This brief, in the form of an e-book, is a collection of notes that cover elementary and medium level number theory with a target audience of primarily computer science students. It can be used in the number theory portion of a discrete mathematics course, or a course on the mathematical foundations of computer science, or as background material for a cryptography course. Thematically it is split into five areas that map to chapters. The first chapter is introductory and covers topics including divisibility, prime numbers, and modular arithmetic including modular linear equations. The second chapter covers additional topics such as Euler's totient function, units and inverses, the Chinese remainder theorem, and Fermat's and Euler's theorems. The following chapter covers primitive roots, quadratic residues, the Jacobi and Legendre symbols, Gauss's lemma and Eisenstein's theorem, and briefly discusses applications of number theory to cryptography. The fourth chapter is focused on traditional primality testing methods covering Miller's algorithms, Rabin's conversion of a Miller algorithm into a probabilistic primality test algorithm, Solovay-Strassen's algorithm and several other peripheral results including Carmichael numbers and the equivalence of Miller's two algorithms. Finally the last brief chapter can be viewed as an introduction to more advanced elements of number theory and its coverage includes multiplicative functions, the M\"obius function, Dirichlet products and Dirichlet and M\"obius inversions. Different parts of this e-book are for freshman to senior undergraduate students in computing and in particular computer science. Graduate students with limited exposure to number theory can use it to acquire a background suitable for typical cryptography courses at the master's level.
tldr: Lecture notes on elementary and intermediate number theory for computer science students, covering divisibility, modular arithmetic, primality testing, and cryptography basics.
motivation: To provide a self-contained number theory resource for computer science students, supporting courses in discrete mathematics, foundations of computing, or cryptography.
method: The notes are organized into five chapters, each covering standard topics in number theory with a focus on algorithms and applications relevant to computer science.
result: A comprehensive set of lecture notes covering divisibility, primes, modular arithmetic, Euler's theorem, Chinese remainder theorem, quadratic residues, primality testing algorithms (Miller, Rabin, Solovay-Strassen), and an introduction to multiplicative functions and Dirichlet convolution.
conclusion: The notes serve as a pedagogical tool for computer science students to acquire the number theory background needed for cryptography and related fields.

title: Krein's Formula For Conic Laplacians On Compact Riemann Surfaces
authors: Liou Jia-Ming (frank)
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish Krein's formula for self-adjoint extensions of conic Laplacians on compact Riemann surfaces. Our approach is based on the finite-dimensional symplectic space of critical asymptotic boundary data: self-adjoint extensions are parametrized by Lagrangian subspaces, and the resolvent difference of two extensions is expressed in terms of the associated Weyl function. We further derive a trace identity for the resolvent difference and use it to prove a comparison formula for the positive-spectrum zeta determinants associated with different Lagrangian boundary conditions, including the contributions of negative eigenvalues and zero modes.
tldr: This paper establishes Krein's formula for conic Laplacians on compact Riemann surfaces, focusing on spectral theory and zeta determinants.
motivation: To extend Krein's formula to conic Laplacians on Riemann surfaces, enabling comparison of spectral invariants under different boundary conditions.
method: Uses finite-dimensional symplectic space of critical asymptotic boundary data, parametrizes self-adjoint extensions by Lagrangian subspaces, and expresses resolvent differences via Weyl functions.
result: Derives a trace identity for resolvent differences and a comparison formula for positive-spectrum zeta determinants, including contributions from negative eigenvalues and zero modes.
conclusion: Provides a spectral theoretic framework for conic Laplacians with applications to geometric analysis and mathematical physics.

title: A Coupled Conforming-Nonconforming Galerkin Method For Poisson's Equation On Curved Domains
authors: Wenju Zhao Qingguang Guan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20985v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A coupled conforming-nonconforming Galerkin method is proposed for Poisson's equation on two-dimensional curved domains. The method applies a weak Galerkin discretization only on a thin boundary layer of curvilinear elements near the curved boundary, while using a standard continuous Galerkin discretization in the polygonal interior. In this way, geometric flexibility is retained where it is needed most, and the number of nonconforming degrees of freedom is significantly reduced. A key ingredient is a mixed interpolation-projection operator on curvilinear weak Galerkin elements, combining [MATH] edge projections with conforming nodal interpolation on the interface side to ensure compatibility with the continuous Galerkin trace. Based on this construction, we prove an optimal a priori error estimate of order [MATH] in the energy norm under the basic geometric assumptions of the method, and an optimal [MATH] estimate of order [MATH] under the additional elliptic dual regularity assumption. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical rates and demonstrate substantial savings in degrees of freedom compared with a fully weak Galerkin discretization.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical method for solving Poisson's equation on curved domains using a coupled conforming-nonconforming Galerkin approach.
motivation: To efficiently handle curved boundaries in finite element methods while reducing computational cost compared to fully nonconforming discretizations.
method: A weak Galerkin discretization is applied only on a thin boundary layer of curvilinear elements, while a standard continuous Galerkin method is used in the interior, with a mixed interpolation-projection operator ensuring compatibility.
result: Optimal a priori error estimates are proved in the energy norm and L2 norm, and numerical experiments confirm the theoretical rates with significant savings in degrees of freedom.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a practical and efficient approach for solving Poisson's equation on curved domains, balancing geometric flexibility and computational cost.

title: Towards Fewer Control Laws Via Continuous-Time Multiparametric Programming
authors: Efstratios N. Pistikopoulos Lida Lamakani
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21031v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiparametric programming offers a powerful solution to the computational burden of solving optimal control problems repeatedly online. By solving the problem once offline, it yields the optimal control laws as explicit closed-form functions of the initial system state, reducing online execution to a direct evaluation with no iterations required. Most existing works build this idea on a discrete-time foundation, slicing the time horizon into intervals and applying KKT conditions to the resulting algebraic system. This discretization forces a tradeoff: too few intervals and the model fails to capture the true system dynamics, while too many cause the problem size, the number of decision variables, and the number of critical regions to grow rapidly, making both offline preparation and online lookup increasingly expensive. This work develops a multiparametric framework that works directly with the continuous-time problem. Pontryagin's Maximum Principle (PMP) is applied without any model discretization, and the optimal control is recovered as an explicit function of the initial state. Compared to the discrete-time formulation, the continuous-time approach produces substantially fewer critical regions, and this number remains fixed regardless of accuracy requirements, since it reflects the structure of the problem itself rather than a discretization grid. The framework also yields the switching times as explicit functions of the initial state, directly exposing when and how the optimal control structure changes over the horizon. Knowing these switching times in advance allows the real-time controller to skip unnecessary computations between them, further reducing the online execution cost. Results from a PAROC framework case study demonstrate that the continuous-time multiparametric approach is a rigorous alternative to the conventional discrete-time formulations.
tldr: This paper presents a continuous-time multiparametric programming framework for optimal control, reducing the number of critical regions compared to discrete-time methods.
motivation: Discrete-time multiparametric programming suffers from a tradeoff between accuracy and problem size, leading to many critical regions. The authors aim to avoid discretization by working directly in continuous time.
method: Pontryagin's Maximum Principle is applied without model discretization to derive optimal control laws as explicit functions of the initial state, and switching times are also obtained explicitly.
result: The continuous-time approach yields substantially fewer critical regions that remain fixed regardless of accuracy requirements, and switching times are known in advance, reducing online computation.
conclusion: Continuous-time multiparametric programming is a rigorous alternative to discrete-time formulations for optimal control.

title: An Efficient Laguerre Minimum Action Method For Computing Quasi-Potentials
authors: Shenghe Huang, Yishuang Yue, Haijun Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21114v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Minimum action methods provide a powerful framework for analyzing rare transitions in small-noise-driven dynamical systems, but their practical performance is often limited by time truncation and parameter sensitivity in infinite-horizon problems. In this paper, we develop an efficient Laguerre spectral minimum action method (LMAM) for computing quasi-potentials associated with fixed points of dynamical systems. Based on the large deviation framework, the method computes minimum action paths by formulating the problem on a semi-infinite time interval and discretize the temporal direction using Laguerre functions. An appropriate time rescaling strategy is proposed to enhance accuracy and convergence of the Laguerre spectral approximation. To efficiently handle nonlinear terms, we employ an improved procedure for evaluating Laguerre--Gauss--Radau quadrature, which enables stable and accurate double-precision computations with a large number of Laguerre modes. Precise numerical analysis for the linear problem and a local result for the nonlinear case are developed. Numerical experiments including both ordinary and partial differential equations (Allen-Cahn and Navier-Stokes) are presented to illustrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method.
tldr: This paper develops a numerical method for computing quasi-potentials in dynamical systems using Laguerre spectral methods.
motivation: Minimum action methods for rare transitions suffer from time truncation and parameter sensitivity; a more efficient and accurate method is needed.
method: The authors propose a Laguerre spectral minimum action method (LMAM) that discretizes the semi-infinite time interval with Laguerre functions and includes a time rescaling strategy and improved quadrature.
