result: Numerical experiments on ODEs and PDEs (Allen-Cahn, Navier-Stokes) demonstrate accuracy and efficiency of the LMAM.
conclusion: The LMAM provides a robust and efficient approach for computing quasi-potentials in small-noise dynamical systems.

title: Distributed-memory Parallelization Of B-spline Based S-version Of The Finite Element Method Via Weighted Graph Abstraction
authors: Nozomi Magome, Naoki Morita, Shigeki Kaneko, Naoto Mitsume
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21142v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To extend the B-spline based s-version of the finite element method (BSFEM), which enables locally high-resolution analysis, to large-scale simulations, domain-decomposition-based parallel computation on distributed-memory systems is indispensable. However, the highly complex interactions induced by the spatial overlap of independent meshes make the construction of interprocessor communication structures extremely challenging, thereby posing a major obstacle to the application of conventional domain decomposition approaches. In this study, we propose a method that mathematically generalizes and simplifies the complex connectivity arising from the physical overlap of meshes as a weighted graph. By reducing the problem to graph theory, we successfully construct a domain-decomposition-based parallelization algorithm for BSFEM and SFEM-based methods with complex mesh structures in distributed-memory environments. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, numerical verification is performed using the three-dimensional steady Poisson equation, confirming the realization of parallel computation in a distributed-memory environment. Furthermore, we demonstrate that assigning weights to graph nodes effectively distributes localized computational loads and substantially reduces the total computational time. The graph-theoretic approach established in this study not only enables the parallelization of BSFEM and SFEM-based methods, but also provides a general theoretical foundation for designing parallelization strategies for other methods with complex communication structures.
tldr: This paper presents a distributed-memory parallelization method for the B-spline based s-version of the finite element method using weighted graph abstraction.
motivation: The complex interactions from overlapping meshes in BSFEM make conventional domain decomposition difficult, hindering large-scale simulations.
method: The authors model the connectivity of overlapping meshes as a weighted graph and apply graph theory to design a domain-decomposition-based parallelization algorithm.
result: Numerical tests on the 3D steady Poisson equation confirm successful parallel computation and show that weighting graph nodes reduces computational time.
conclusion: The graph-theoretic approach provides a general foundation for parallelizing methods with complex communication structures.

title: Duet: Decentralized Bilevel Optimization Without Lower-Level Strong Convexity
authors: Zhen Qin, Zhuqing Liu, Songtao Lu, Yingbin Liang, Jia Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21153v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decentralized bilevel optimization (DBO) provides a powerful framework for multi-agent systems to solve local bilevel tasks in a decentralized fashion without the need for a central server. However, most existing DBO methods rely on lower-level strong convexity (LLSC) to guarantee unique solutions and a well-defined hypergradient for stationarity measure, hindering their applicability in many practical scenarios not satisfying LLSC. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a new single-loop DBO algorithm called diminishing quadratically-regularized bilevel decentralized optimization (DUET), which eliminates the need for LLSC by introducing a diminishing quadratic regularization to the lower-level (LL) objective. We show that DUET achieves an iteration complexity of [MATH] for approximate KKT-stationary point convergence under relaxed assumptions, where [MATH] and [MATH] are control parameters for LL learning rate and averaging, respectively. In addition, our DUET algorithm incorporates gradient tracking to address data heterogeneity, a key challenge in DBO settings. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to tackle DBO without LLSC under decentralized settings with data heterogeneity. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the practical effectiveness of our proposed algorithms.
tldr: This paper proposes a decentralized bilevel optimization algorithm that does not require lower-level strong convexity.
motivation: Existing decentralized bilevel optimization methods rely on lower-level strong convexity, limiting their applicability; this work aims to remove that assumption.
method: The authors introduce a single-loop algorithm with diminishing quadratic regularization on the lower-level objective and gradient tracking to handle data heterogeneity.
result: The algorithm achieves iteration complexity for approximate KKT-stationary point convergence under relaxed assumptions, and numerical experiments validate its effectiveness.
conclusion: This is the first work to tackle decentralized bilevel optimization without lower-level strong convexity, broadening the applicability of DBO.

title: A Multi-Objective Approach To Curriculum-Based Course Timetabling With Continuity Across Semesters
authors: Florian Meier, Thomas Stidsen, Clemens Thielen, Andreas Wiese
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21176v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a curriculum-based university course timetabling problem in which the preferences of two key stakeholder groups - lecturers and students - must be balanced while maintaining continuity across semesters in a weekly repeating timetable. While existing approaches typically rely on single-objective formulations or aggregate multiple objectives into a weighted sum, this can obscure the underlying trade-offs between conflicting stakeholder preferences. We therefore propose a multi-objective mixed-integer programming approach that explicitly separates lecturer and student objectives and incorporates timetable continuity by limiting the number of changes, called perturbations, in the time period assignments of selected courses relative to the corresponding semester of the previous academic year. To explore the resulting trade-offs, we develop a multi-objective solution approach based on the lexicographic [MATH]-constraint method, enabling the computation of a representative set of solutions whose images, i.e., their vectors of objective values, cover different regions of the objective space. The approach is evaluated on real-world instances from the Straubing Campus of the Technical University of Munich. The computational results reveal a clear and consistent trade-off between lecturers' and students' objectives across all instances. Moreover, the number of allowed perturbations is identified as a key decision parameter: relaxing this constraint significantly improves timetable quality for both stakeholder groups, although diminishing returns are observed beyond certain thresholds. Overall, the proposed approach provides decision support by generating a diverse set of optimized timetables and enabling a transparent analysis of stakeholder trade-offs and continuity for the practical timetable planning process.
tldr: This paper addresses a curriculum-based university course timetabling problem using multi-objective optimization, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Existing timetabling approaches often use single-objective or weighted-sum methods that obscure trade-offs between lecturer and student preferences, and they lack continuity across semesters.
method: The authors propose a multi-objective mixed-integer programming approach with a lexicographic epsilon-constraint method to generate a representative set of solutions balancing lecturer and student objectives while limiting timetable perturbations.
result: Computational results on real-world instances show a clear trade-off between lecturer and student objectives, and allowing more perturbations improves timetable quality for both groups with diminishing returns.
conclusion: The approach provides decision support by generating diverse optimized timetables and enabling transparent analysis of stakeholder trade-offs and continuity.

title: A semi-Lagrangian Method For The Polyatomic Esbgk Model
authors: Klaas Willems, Erik Arlemark, Giovanni Samaey, Axel Klar
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21191v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Polyatomic kinetic models are essential for accurately capturing the thermodynamic behavior of real gases, as internal energy modes significantly influence transport coefficients, relaxation processes, and non-equilibrium effects that cannot be represented by monoatomic models. The polyatomic ESBGK model describes molecular collisions as a relaxation towards a generalized Gaussian distribution with an anisotropic covariance matrix and an exponentially decaying internal energy distribution. We present a new semi-Lagrangian scheme for the polyatomic Ellipsoidal Statistical BGK (ESBGK) model of the Boltzmann equation. The semi-Lagrangian framework, being deterministic and grid-based, removes the time-step restriction associated with the linear transport term by following the method of characteristics. The potentially stiff relaxation term is treated using an implicit A-stable linear multistep method which, owing to the structure of the BGK operator, can be reformulated into a cheap time-stepping scheme. This yields a highly efficient and numerically stable method. The numerical method is asymptotic preserving and stiffly accurate, meaning the scheme asymptotically converges to a scheme for the Euler equations in the vanishing Knudsen limit. In addition, we prove that the first-order scheme, asymptotically converges to the compressible Navier-Stokes equation with correct transport coefficients. Finally, we propose inflow and outflow boundary conditions suitable for BGK-type kinetic equations. We perform simulations of the Fourier and Couette test case to compare the BGK model with Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC). To conclude, we demonstrate the method on a challenging orifice flow test case with moving boundaries.
tldr: This paper presents a semi-Lagrangian numerical scheme for the polyatomic ESBGK model of the Boltzmann equation, focusing on computational fluid dynamics for rarefied gas flows.
motivation: Accurate simulation of polyatomic gases is important for capturing non-equilibrium effects in rarefied flows, but existing numerical methods are computationally expensive or have time-step restrictions.
method: A semi-Lagrangian scheme is developed that removes the CFL condition by following characteristics, and the stiff relaxation term is treated implicitly with an A-stable linear multistep method, resulting in an asymptotic-preserving scheme.
result: The scheme is shown to be asymptotic-preserving and stiffly accurate, converging to the Euler and Navier-Stokes equations in the appropriate limits. Simulations of Fourier and Couette flows and an orifice flow demonstrate accuracy and efficiency.
conclusion: The proposed semi-Lagrangian method provides an efficient and stable numerical approach for simulating polyatomic rarefied gas flows using the ESBGK model.

title: Borel Complexity Of Isometry Classes Of $\mathcal{C}(K)$ Spaces With Countable Compacta
authors: Marek C\'uth, Martin Dole\v{z}al, Ond\v{r}ej Kurka, Jakub Rondo\v{s}
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21204v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every countable compact space [MATH], we determine the exact Borel complexity of the isometry class of the Banach space [MATH]. As a byproduct, we also determine the precise Borel complexity of the homeomorphism class of a fixed countable compact space [MATH], improving earlier results of Cenzer and Mauldin. The above results provide concrete and natural examples of sets with arbitrarily high, still exactly determined, Borel complexity. Moreover, we find a new characterization of those real [MATH]-preduals that are isometric to [MATH] for some zero-dimensional compact space [MATH] and we determine the precise Borel complexity of [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies the Borel complexity of isometry classes of Banach spaces C(K) for countable compact K, a topic in descriptive set theory and functional analysis.
motivation: To determine the exact Borel complexity of isometry classes of C(K) spaces and homeomorphism classes of countable compact spaces, improving previous results.
method: Uses descriptive set theory and Banach space theory to classify the complexity of these classes in the Borel hierarchy.
result: Provides exact Borel complexity for each countable compact K, and characterizes real L1-preduals isometric to C(K) for zero-dimensional compact K.
conclusion: The results give concrete examples of sets with arbitrarily high but exactly determined Borel complexity.

title: A Fully Discrete Active Flux Method For The Euler Equations Comparing Different Truly Multi-dimensional Evolution Operators
authors: Amelie Porfetye Christiane Helzel
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article builds upon our recently published fully discrete Cartesian grid Active Flux method for the Euler equations by introducing a new evolution operator for the linearized Euler equations. The evolution of the point value degrees of freedom located at grid cell boundaries and used to compute numerical fluxes is a key component of fully discrete Active Flux methods. Our methods are based on local linearizations of the Euler equations and the use of truly multi-dimensional evolution operators for these linearized problems. Here, we propose to solve the linearized Euler equations in moving coordinates, reducing them to acoustics, which can be solved exactly. We compare this approach with our previous one, in which we used approximate evolution operators derived using the method of bicharacteristics. The moving-grid approach is closely related to recent methods proposed by Barsukow as well as Duraisamy. Our choice of local linearization, as well as correction of linearization errors, enables us to construct third-order accurate methods for smooth solutions of the nonlinear Euler equations. Numerical results illustrate the performance of these methods for different flow regimes, ranging from discontinuous solution structures with shock waves to vortex structures in the low Mach number regime.
tldr: This paper presents a fully discrete Active Flux method for the Euler equations, comparing different multi-dimensional evolution operators.
motivation: To improve the accuracy and robustness of numerical methods for solving the Euler equations in computational fluid dynamics.
method: The method uses local linearizations of the Euler equations and solves them in moving coordinates to obtain exact solutions for acoustics, compared with approximate evolution operators from the method of bicharacteristics.
result: The moving-grid approach yields third-order accurate methods for smooth solutions and performs well across various flow regimes including shocks and low Mach number vortices.
conclusion: The proposed evolution operator based on moving coordinates is a viable alternative for constructing high-order Active Flux methods.

title: On Significant Pointwise Contractions And Annular Contractions
authors: Ovidiu Popescu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the current paper, we introduce the class of . This family of mappings extends the classical Banach contractions and also contains nonexpansive mappings. We prove that in a complete metric space every significant pointwise contraction admits a fixed point that can be approximated through Picard iterations. We provide examples showing that the newly introduced class differs from the class of piecewise contractions and is not contained in it. Moreover, we point out that significant pointwise contractions are continuous and may possess multiple fixed points. We further introduce the class of , which generalizes the class of shrinkings, and prove that any such mapping has a fixed point in a compact metric space. Moreover, we define the class of , which includes Banach contractions but is distinct from the class of Suzuki mappings. Finally, we obtain a fixed point theorem for annular pointwise contractions and present an additional condition ensuring the existence of fixed points.
tldr: The paper introduces new classes of contractive mappings in metric spaces and proves fixed point theorems.
motivation: To extend classical Banach contractions and nonexpansive mappings to broader classes for fixed point theory.
method: Defines significant pointwise contractions, annular contractions, and related mappings; uses Picard iterations and compactness arguments.
result: Proves existence of fixed points for these mappings under completeness or compactness conditions, with examples showing distinctness from known classes.
conclusion: The new contraction classes generalize existing ones and yield fixed point theorems, but the work is purely mathematical with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Restart And Adaptive Acceleration In Stochastic Gradient Methods
authors: Ali Elhishi, Chistophe Roux, Alexandre D'aspremont
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21354v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study restart schemes in stochastic optimization problems for non-smooth and weakly convex that satisfy a Kurdyka-\L ojasiewicz inequality. We show that using restarts allows us to leverage the K{\L} inequalities to achieve improved rates of convergence, with acceleration depending explicitly on the K{\L} exponent. Furthermore, optimal restart schedules lead to learning-rates akin to Polyak steps for SGD. While regularity constants such as the K{\L} exponent are typically unknown in practice, we prove that restart schemes are robust to a significant misspecification of these constants, hence nearly adaptive. We detail numerical experiments on both toy problems, where the K{\L} exponent is controlled, and training of Large Language Models (LLMs).
tldr: This paper studies restart and adaptive acceleration in stochastic gradient methods for non-smooth weakly convex optimization with Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz inequality.
motivation: To improve convergence rates of stochastic gradient methods for non-smooth weakly convex problems using restarts, and to achieve adaptivity without knowing regularity constants.
method: The authors propose restart schemes that leverage the Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz inequality to accelerate convergence, and analyze robustness to misspecification of the KL exponent.
result: Restart schemes achieve improved rates depending on the KL exponent, and are robust to misspecification, leading to adaptive learning rates similar to Polyak steps.
conclusion: Restart schemes provide a practical and robust acceleration for stochastic optimization, with numerical validation on toy problems and LLM training.

title: Inverse Source Problems For A Class Of Fractional Elliptic Equations With Singular Coefficients
authors: Zewen Wang, Liang Guo, Shufang Qiu, Bin Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21375v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An inverse source problem for a class of fractional elliptic equations with singular coefficients is investigated in this paper. For the corresponding direct problem, a formal solution is derived and the well-posedness of the solution is established. For the inverse problem, a H\"older-type conditional stability estimate is obtained in a Hilbert scale associated with exponential operators. Based on this stability framework, two regularization methods are proposed for reconstructing the unknown source term: the exponential-type Tikhonov regularization method and the exponential quasi-boundary value regularization method. Convergence estimates for the regularized solutions are derived under both a priori and a posteriori choices of the regularization parameter. In addition, finite-dimensional spectral approximation results show that the proposed methods are also applicable to general square-integrable source terms, without requiring the exact source to satisfy an exponential-type source condition. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed methods provide stable and accurate reconstructions for both smooth and piecewise smooth sources even under low signal-to-noise ratio conditions.
tldr: This paper studies inverse source problems for fractional elliptic equations with singular coefficients, using regularization methods for reconstruction.
motivation: Inverse source problems arise in many applications such as medical imaging and geophysics, and fractional elliptic equations model anomalous diffusion.
method: The authors derive a formal solution for the direct problem, obtain a Hölder-type conditional stability estimate, and propose exponential-type Tikhonov and quasi-boundary value regularization methods.
result: Convergence estimates are derived under a priori and a posteriori parameter choices, and spectral approximation shows applicability to general square-integrable sources.
conclusion: The proposed methods provide stable and accurate reconstructions for smooth and piecewise smooth sources even under low signal-to-noise ratio.

title: Finite-Horizon Portfolio Choice, Labor Supply, And Early Retirement Under Borrowing Constraints
authors: Gugyum Ha, Junkee Jeon, Jihoon Ok
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a finite-horizon optimal consumption and portfolio problem with labor supply flexibility and an irreversible early retirement option under a borrowing constraint. The agent chooses consumption, risky investment, and leisure before retirement, while after retirement labor income disappears and leisure is fixed at its maximal level. Preferences are described by a Cobb--Douglas utility, and wealth must remain nonnegative. {Using a dual martingale method, we transform the primal problem into a zero-sum stopper--singular-controller game. The associated dual value is characterized by a min--max parabolic variational inequality with obstacle and gradient constraints. We show that the maximal strong solution of the resulting variational inequality is the unique admissible strong solution whose gradient-constrained free boundary, namely the binding boundary, is monotone increasing in calendar time. A verification argument then identifies this strong solution with the value of the stopper--singular-controller game, and duality recovers the optimal retirement, consumption, leisure, and portfolio policies.} The numerical analysis recovers the value function and optimal policies, and illustrates how labor supply flexibility affects consumption, portfolio choice, and retirement timing under borrowing constraints.
tldr: This paper studies optimal consumption, portfolio choice, and labor supply with early retirement under borrowing constraints using a dual martingale method.
motivation: To understand how borrowing constraints and labor flexibility affect consumption, investment, and retirement decisions in a finite-horizon setting.
method: Uses a dual martingale method to transform the problem into a zero-sum stopper–singular-controller game, characterized by a min–max parabolic variational inequality with obstacle and gradient constraints.
result: Shows the maximal strong solution of the variational inequality is unique and its free boundary is monotone increasing in time; numerical analysis recovers optimal policies.
conclusion: Labor supply flexibility significantly impacts consumption, portfolio choice, and retirement timing under borrowing constraints.

title: An FFT-based Solver With General Boundary Conditions For Stationary Diffusion Problems Based On Chebyshev Collocation
authors: Javier Segurado Juan M. Quecedo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21410v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An efficient and robust FFT-based solver is proposed for diffusion-type problems with general Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions, based on a Chebyshev collocation framework. The method combines Chebyshev polynomial approximations with FFT-based operators to provide a matrix-free implementation of the discrete differential operator at the Chebyshev-Gauss-Lobatto points. The linear system of equations resulting from the Chebyshev discretization is solved using LGMRES. To overcome convergence problems on fine grids, a hierarchical refinement strategy based on modal prolongation is proposed, enabling the solution of very large 3D problems. The methodology is applicable to homogeneous and heterogeneous domains, as well as to linear and nonlinear constitutive equations. The accuracy of the proposed method is analyzed by solving the Poisson equation in homogeneous 1D and 3D domains with general boundary conditions, using manufactured analytical solutions as references. Convergence to the analytical solution is achieved in a few iterations, with smaller errors than those obtained using DCT/DST approaches. Discretizations of up to [MATH] are achieved thanks to the hierarchical refinement strategy. In the case of heterogeneous domains, the accuracy and efficiency obtained are similar to those of a standard periodic FFT approach. It is found that the computational complexity of the method preserves the FFT scaling, of order [MATH], in all the cases studied.
tldr: This paper presents an FFT-based solver for stationary diffusion problems using Chebyshev collocation with general boundary conditions.
motivation: To develop an efficient and robust numerical method for diffusion-type problems that can handle general Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions, overcoming limitations of periodic FFT approaches.
method: The method combines Chebyshev polynomial approximations with FFT-based operators for a matrix-free implementation, solves the linear system with LGMRES, and uses a hierarchical refinement strategy based on modal prolongation for fine grids.
result: The solver achieves convergence to analytical solutions in few iterations with smaller errors than DCT/DST approaches, handles up to 512^3 discretizations, and preserves FFT scaling complexity.
conclusion: The proposed method is accurate and efficient for homogeneous and heterogeneous domains with general boundary conditions, suitable for large 3D problems.

title: Commentary On Askey's Szego Paper
authors: Barry Simon
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21477v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An expository note about the paper Askey wrote on Szego's 60th anniversary about the later's work.
tldr: An expository note on Askey's commentary on Szego's work, unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: To provide historical and mathematical context for Askey's paper on Szego's contributions.
method: Expository writing, summarizing and commenting on Askey's paper.
result: A commentary note with no new technical results.
conclusion: The note serves as a historical exposition without advancing any of the user's research directions.

title: Unified Ergodic Primal-Dual Gap Rates With Unhalved Primal Stepsizes
authors: Ming Yan Sirong Dai
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study ergodic primal-dual gap rates for first-order primal-dual methods applied to \[ \min_x f(x)+g(x)+h(Ax), \] where [MATH] is smooth and convex, [MATH] and [MATH] are proper, closed, convex functions, and [MATH] is linear. Standard gap-rate proofs often impose the halved smooth-stepsize condition [MATH], even though the corresponding convergence theory allows the larger range [MATH]. We introduce a residual-to-gap transfer principle: positive residual terms in the one-step gap inequality are controlled by the decrease of a Lyapunov function. This yields [MATH] ergodic primal-dual gap bounds with the unhalved primal stepsize [MATH] for Condat--V\~u, PD3O, AFBA/PDDY, and PAPC/PDFP[MATH]O, under their algorithm-dependent product conditions. We also give a two-dimensional counterexample showing that the fully separated rectangle [MATH], [MATH] cannot hold in the general three-function setting.
tldr: This paper proves ergodic primal-dual gap rates for first-order optimization methods with unhalved primal stepsizes.
motivation: Standard proofs for primal-dual methods require a halved stepsize condition, but convergence theory allows larger stepsizes; the authors aim to close this gap.
method: They introduce a residual-to-gap transfer principle that controls positive residual terms via Lyapunov function decrease, and apply it to several algorithms (Condat-Vũ, PD3O, AFBA/PDDY, PAPC/PDFP²O).
result: They obtain O(1/k) ergodic primal-dual gap bounds with unhalved primal stepsizes under algorithm-dependent product conditions, and provide a counterexample showing the fully separated rectangle condition cannot hold in general.
conclusion: The work extends theoretical guarantees for primal-dual methods, but is purely in convex optimization with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: A Note On The Convergence Guarantees Of RLT-based Algorithms For Polynomial Optimization
authors: Alejandro Barros-Gonz\'alez, Julio Gonz\'alez-D\'iaz, Brais Gonz\'alez-Rodr\'iguez, Iria Rodr\'iguez Acevedo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper identifies and addresses a mathematical oversight in one of the foundational results on the Reformulation-Linearization Technique (RLT) for polynomial optimization. We then argue that, although correctness of the original result can be easily recovered by adding a minor and natural assumption, not being aware of this nuance may lead to the loss of convergence guarantees in RLT-based algorithms.
tldr: This paper addresses a mathematical oversight in the convergence guarantees of RLT-based algorithms for polynomial optimization.
motivation: The authors identify a flaw in a foundational result of the Reformulation-Linearization Technique (RLT) for polynomial optimization, which could affect the convergence guarantees of RLT-based algorithms.
method: The paper analyzes the original proof, pinpoints the oversight, and shows that adding a minor assumption restores correctness.
result: The oversight is corrected, and the convergence guarantees are recovered under a natural additional assumption.
conclusion: Practitioners should be aware of this nuance to ensure the validity of RLT-based algorithms.

title: Reference-Free, Long-Horizon Trajectory Optimization For Aggressive Autonomous Driving In Milliseconds
authors: Prayag Sharma, Jonathan Y. M. Goh, Franck Djeumou
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous vehicles must generate long-horizon and dynamically feasible trajectories in real time-even when operating at the limits of vehicle handling-to ensure safe operation in adverse conditions. However, existing work rarely quantifies the computational demands of generating such trajectories without prior references, warm starts and often defaults to low-fidelity models, compromising accuracy and control authority. We investigate the modeling and solver design choices that enable real-time solution of long-horizon, reference-free optimal control problems (OCPs) using full vehicle dynamics. To this end, we analyze vehicle stiffness properties to justify the OCP's integration scheme and show that lower-order A-stable methods consistently outperform alternatives, with solve time differences reaching two orders of magnitude. We show that robust nonlinear solver performance hinges on understanding barrier parameter update strategies and safeguarding techniques for Hessian indefiniteness, inherent in some interior point methods. Lastly, we propose a computationally efficient method for generating initial guesses using dynamic equilibrium, unlocking real-time performance and reducing initial infeasibility by up to four orders of magnitude. Extensive benchmarking and high-fidelity BeamNG simulation demonstrate compute times as low as 55 ms over a 260 m horizon, including high-speed obstacle avoidance scenarios where drifting emerges as a necessary component of feasible trajectory generation.
tldr: This paper presents a method for real-time, reference-free trajectory optimization for aggressive autonomous driving using full vehicle dynamics.
motivation: Autonomous vehicles need to generate long-horizon, dynamically feasible trajectories in real time, especially at handling limits, but existing work lacks computational efficiency without warm starts.
method: The authors analyze vehicle stiffness to choose an integration scheme, use lower-order A-stable methods, robust nonlinear solver techniques, and a dynamic equilibrium-based initial guess generation.
result: The approach achieves compute times as low as 55 ms over a 260 m horizon in high-fidelity simulations, including drifting maneuvers.
conclusion: Real-time, reference-free trajectory optimization is feasible with appropriate modeling and solver choices, enabling safe autonomous driving in adverse conditions.

title: Accelerated And Stable Convergence With Anchored Optimistic Method
authors: Motahareh Sohrabi, Jianxin You, Simon Lacoste-Julien, Eduard Gorbunov, Gauthier Gidel
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study first-order methods for solving monotone variational inequalities arising in min-max optimization. Classical approaches such as the extragradient method rely on two gradient queries per iteration, which limits their analysis and applicability in the online and stochastic settings. We propose a family of Generalized Optimistic Methods with Anchoring (GOMA), which combine two-time-scale optimistic updates with an anchoring term inspired by Halpern iteration. In the deterministic setting, GOMA achieves the optimal accelerated last-iterate rate [MATH] on the squared gradient norm for monotone Lipschitz operators. In the stochastic setting with unbounded variance, a simplified single-call variant of GOMA achieves a last-iterate convergence rate of [MATH] on the squared gradient norm. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first such guarantee for stochastic monotone Lipschitz variational inequalities in the unconstrained setting without variance reduction or growing batches.
tldr: This paper proposes a family of generalized optimistic methods with anchoring for solving monotone variational inequalities, achieving accelerated convergence rates in deterministic and stochastic settings.
motivation: Classical extragradient methods require two gradient queries per iteration, limiting their applicability in online and stochastic settings. The authors aim to design a single-call method with optimal convergence guarantees.
method: The authors combine two-time-scale optimistic updates with an anchoring term inspired by Halpern iteration to create the GOMA family. They analyze deterministic and stochastic variants, including a simplified single-call version for unbounded variance.
result: GOMA achieves optimal accelerated last-iterate rate O(1/k^2) on squared gradient norm for deterministic monotone Lipschitz operators. The stochastic variant achieves O(1/k) rate without variance reduction or growing batches.
conclusion: The proposed methods provide the first last-iterate convergence guarantees for stochastic monotone variational inequalities in the unconstrained setting, improving upon existing approaches.

title: An Aubin-Nitsche Lemma For A Positivity-preserving Finite Element Method
authors: Theophile Chaumont-Frelet Gabriel R. Barrenechea
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we prove an Aubin-Nitsche Lemma for a positivity-preserving discretisation of an elliptic problem. Due to the nonlinearity of the discretisation, the result requires as a first step the proposal of a linearised adjoint problem that can be linked to the method of choice by appropriately selecting weights. This linearised adjoint problem, together with a regularity result, allow the proof of an optimal-order error estimate in the [MATH]-norm of the error.
tldr: This paper proves an Aubin-Nitsche lemma for a positivity-preserving finite element method for elliptic problems.
motivation: To obtain optimal-order error estimates in the L2 norm for a nonlinear positivity-preserving discretization.
method: A linearized adjoint problem is introduced with appropriately chosen weights, and a regularity result is used to derive the error estimate.
result: An optimal-order error estimate in the L2 norm is proved for the positivity-preserving finite element method.
conclusion: The proposed linearized adjoint approach successfully extends the Aubin-Nitsche technique to nonlinear discretizations.

title: On Fixed-Time Stability Of Continuous Dynamics For Non-Monotone Variational Inequalities
authors: Sina Arefizadeh, Kunal Garg, Angelia Nedi\'c
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-monotone variational inequalities (NMVI) are an important class of problems that generalize non-convex optimization and have various applications in optimization theory, machine learning, game theory, and economics, among others. Most existing work on NMVIs focuses on the asymptotic convergence of algorithms proposed to solve these problems. In this paper, we tackle the problems of exponential and fixed-time stability of the solution set of a class of NMVIs for both unconstrained and constrained problems. We first present novel conditions guaranteeing exponential stability of solutions to unconstrained NMVIs for a uniquely constructed dynamical system under mild assumptions on the gradient of the non-monotone map. Then, under similar assumptions, we construct another novel dynamical system whose equilibrium point is fixed-time stable, i.e., the trajectories reach the equilibrium within a fixed time, independent of the initial conditions. For the case of constrained NMVIs, we employ a continuous-time variant of the Korpelevich method for exponential stability of the solution set, and provide a novel scaling factor in the dynamics to achieve fixed-time stability. We illustrate the efficacy of the proposed modified dynamical systems through numerical simulations and conclude the paper with a brief note on the behavior of the discretized variant of the proposed dynamics and on further work that remains to be done.
tldr: This paper studies fixed-time stability of dynamical systems for solving non-monotone variational inequalities, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Non-monotone variational inequalities generalize non-convex optimization and have applications in machine learning and economics, but existing algorithms only guarantee asymptotic convergence.
method: The authors construct novel dynamical systems and use Lyapunov analysis to prove exponential and fixed-time stability for both unconstrained and constrained NMVIs, employing a continuous-time Korpelevich method for the constrained case.
result: They provide conditions for exponential stability and achieve fixed-time stability with a scaling factor, demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The proposed dynamics offer stronger convergence guarantees (fixed-time) for a class of NMVIs, with potential for discretized variants in future work.

title: Nonsmooth Obstacles And Killed Resolvents In Reflected Stochastic Control
authors: Louis Shuo Wang, Jiguang Yu, Ye Liang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21575v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an infinite-horizon optimal stopping problem for a normally reflected two-dimensional diffusion in the quadrant with nonsmooth max-type payoff \(G(x_1,x_2)=x_1\vee\alpha x_2\). The main novelty is a measure-valued variational formulation: the stopping gain \(\Gamma=c+rG-\mathcal LG\) is shown to be a signed Radon measure whose singular component is supported on the kink diagonal \(\{x_1=\alpha x_2\}\), and this component is computed explicitly. We prove that the value admits the killed-resolvent representation \[ V=G-R_r^{\mathcal C}\Gamma, \] where the reflected diffusion is killed upon entry into the stopping set. This corrects the generally invalid unrestricted-resolvent formula. Under explicit monotonicity hypotheses, the stopping set has epigraph form, and the free boundary is characterized by a killed-potential trace condition. A verification theorem certifies locally Lipschitz candidate boundaries as optimal.
tldr: This paper studies an optimal stopping problem for reflected diffusions with nonsmooth payoff, using measure-valued variational formulations and killed-resolvent representations.
motivation: To solve optimal stopping problems for reflected diffusions in domains with nonsmooth boundaries, where standard resolvent formulas fail.
method: The authors develop a measure-valued variational formulation, showing the stopping gain is a signed Radon measure with singular component on the kink diagonal, and derive a killed-resolvent representation for the value function.
result: The value function is expressed as G minus the killed resolvent of the gain measure, and under monotonicity conditions the stopping set has epigraph form with a free boundary characterized by a killed-potential trace condition.
conclusion: The killed-resolvent representation corrects the invalid unrestricted-resolvent formula, and a verification theorem certifies locally Lipschitz candidate boundaries as optimal.

title: Convergence Analysis Of Muon-type Methods With Inexact Lmo In The Degenerate Case
authors: Peter Richt\'arik Xun Qian
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21581v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Muon-type methods have demonstrated potentially superior performance over Adam and its variants, and have shown hyperparameter transferability across model sizes when specific norms are chosen for the LMO in deep architectures. However, while the LMO is solved approximately via iterative algorithms in practice, most convergence analyses consider the ideal case where the search direction is the exact solution to the LMO. Recently, the inexact Muon update was analyzed by Shulgin et al. [2025], which reveals a fundamental coupling between the inexactness and the optimal step size and momentum. However, the convergence is guaranteed for the non-degenerate case only, i.e., the smallest positive singular value of the rescaled momentum is assumed to be bounded below by some positive constant when the spectral norm is used. In this work, we investigate Muon-type methods with inexact LMO in the degenerate case, where the smallest positive singular value of the rescaled momentum can approach zero, for the general non-convex case and the star-convex case with weight decay. Novel assumptions are proposed to address the challenges posed by inexact LMO in such degenerate scenarios, and convergence rates are established under the layer-wise [MATH]-smooth assumption for both cases.
tldr: This paper analyzes convergence of Muon-type optimization methods with inexact linear minimization oracle in degenerate cases for non-convex and star-convex objectives.
motivation: Muon-type methods show promise in deep learning but existing convergence analyses assume non-degenerate conditions; this work addresses the realistic degenerate case where singular values can approach zero.
method: The authors propose novel assumptions to handle inexact LMO in degenerate scenarios and derive convergence rates under layer-wise smoothness for general non-convex and star-convex cases with weight decay.
result: Convergence rates are established for both non-convex and star-convex settings under degenerate conditions, extending prior work that only covered non-degenerate cases.
conclusion: The analysis provides theoretical guarantees for Muon-type methods in more practical degenerate settings, supporting their use in deep learning optimization.

title: Unbounded Bunching Of Saddle Connections On The Golden L
authors: Benjamin Dozier
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show there is a translation surface (the golden L) that has unbounded bunching: for every positive integer K there exists a ball B of radius 1 in R^2 that contains at least K vectors that are periods of saddle connections on this surface.
tldr: This paper proves unbounded bunching of saddle connection periods on the golden L translation surface.
motivation: Understanding the distribution of saddle connection periods on translation surfaces is a fundamental problem in dynamical systems and geometry.
method: The author constructs explicit sequences of saddle connections on the golden L surface and shows that their period vectors cluster arbitrarily densely in a ball.
result: For any integer K, there exists a radius-1 ball in R^2 containing at least K period vectors of saddle connections.
conclusion: The golden L surface exhibits unbounded bunching, a phenomenon not previously known for translation surfaces.

title: A Spherical Harmonic Pseudo-spectral Approach To Mean Curvature Flow Of Surfaces With Spherical Topology
authors: Genming Bai
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose and analyze a spherical harmonic pseudo-spectral method for the mean curvature flow of closed surfaces with spherical topology. The evolving surface is represented by a global parametrization over the unit sphere, and the continuous weak formulation underlying Dziuk's method [G. Dziuk, Numer. Math., 1991] is discretized in a finite-dimensional space of spherical harmonics. By explicitly taking into account quadrature errors on the autonomously evolving numerical surface, we prove exponential convergence of the position error under the assumption that the initial global parametrization is analytic. The convergence analysis developed herein is general and could apply to other moving-domain and geometric evolution problems. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical result.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical method for mean curvature flow of surfaces with spherical topology using spherical harmonics.
motivation: To accurately simulate geometric evolution problems like mean curvature flow, which have applications in image processing and materials science.
method: A spherical harmonic pseudo-spectral method discretizes the weak formulation of mean curvature flow on a global parametrization over the unit sphere.
result: Exponential convergence of the position error is proven under analytic initial parametrization, and numerical experiments confirm the theoretical result.
conclusion: The proposed method is accurate and efficient for mean curvature flow of spherical surfaces, and the analysis framework may extend to other moving-domain problems.

title: Nonlinear Guidance For Arrival Time And Arrival Angle Control Using Trajectory Shaping
authors: Andr\'es Infante Adri\'an Kun Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a nonlinear trajectory shaping guidance strategy for arrival time and angle control of a constant-speed fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicle. The look angle is parameterized by a fourth-order polynomial. The nonlinear guidance problem is transformed into solving two coupled nonlinear integral equations with respect to two unknown guidance parameters. Directly solving these equations is challenging due to the strong coupling between the parameters. To address this, a two-stage solution procedure is developed. In the first stage, an analytical warm start is constructed. Specifically, by applying approximations, a linear relationship between the two guidance parameters is obtained. With this relationship, a scalar quadratic equation in the first guidance parameter is derived, leading to a good initial guess for the first guidance parameter. In the second stage, this initial guess is refined by solving a one-dimensional nonlinear equation. The obtained solution is finally used as the initial guess for solving the original two-dimensional nonlinear system of equations. Numerical simulations demonstrate that for the test cases, the obtained solution is very close to the open-loop optimal solution, even in highly nonlinear scenarios where some existing methods fail to generate a feasible solution.
tldr: This paper presents a nonlinear trajectory shaping guidance strategy for arrival time and angle control of a fixed-wing UAV.
motivation: To achieve precise arrival time and angle control for UAVs in highly nonlinear scenarios where existing methods may fail.
method: The look angle is parameterized by a fourth-order polynomial, transforming the problem into solving coupled nonlinear integral equations via a two-stage procedure with an analytical warm start.
result: Numerical simulations show the solution is very close to the open-loop optimal solution, even in challenging nonlinear cases.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a feasible and near-optimal solution for UAV guidance with arrival time and angle constraints.

title: An Analytic Inversion Formula For The N-dimensional Cylindrical Radon Transform
authors: Fatma Terzioglu Jenna Jones
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21673v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the overdetermined problem of inverting the n-dimensional cylindrical Radon transform, which maps a function to its integrals over cylindrical surfaces. In practice, the cylindrical Radon transform arises in photoacoustic tomography as a measurement model for integrating line detectors. By exploiting its relationship with the Funk and Radon transforms, we derive an analytic inversion formula for the cylindrical Radon transform. We also present numerical implementations of the proposed inversion algorithm, demonstrating its stability.
tldr: This paper derives an analytic inversion formula for the n-dimensional cylindrical Radon transform, with applications in photoacoustic tomography.
motivation: The cylindrical Radon transform arises in photoacoustic tomography with line detectors, and an efficient inversion method is needed for image reconstruction.
method: The authors exploit the relationship between the cylindrical Radon transform, the Funk transform, and the Radon transform to derive an analytic inversion formula.
result: An explicit inversion formula is obtained and numerically implemented, demonstrating stability.
conclusion: The proposed inversion formula provides a stable and efficient method for reconstructing images from cylindrical Radon transform data.

title: Bells-o: Evaluating The Operational Trade-offs Of Llm Supervision Systems
authors: Leonhard Waibl, Felix Michalak, Hadrien Mariaccia
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20668v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM supervision systems, namely input/output moderation filters and jailbreak detectors, are the primary safeguard against misuse in deployed AI applications, yet existing benchmarks are often vendor-biased, omit cost and latency, and rarely compare specialized guardrails against repurposed generalist LLMs. We present BELLS-O (Benchmark for the Evaluation of LLM Supervision Systems, Operational), the first independent operational benchmark of LLM supervision systems. BELLS-O evaluates 28 systems from 17 providers: every major specialized guardrail (e.g., LlamaGuard-4, ShieldGemma-2, Lakera Guard) and frontier generalists repurposed as supervisors (e.g., GPT-5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Grok-4.1), jointly on detection rate, false-positive rate, latency, and monetary cost. We cover input/output moderation across 11 harm categories and jailbreak detection across 13 attack techniques, using in-house datasets built from handcrafted prompts, expert-curated samples, and quality-controlled synthetic generation. To suppress latent generator fingerprints in synthetic data, every generated sample is paraphrased. Mapping the Pareto frontier reveals use-case-dependent tradeoffs. On content moderation, specialized supervisors are operationally dominant: top systems match frontier LLMs on detection (~95% vs. 94%) at comparably low false-positive rates (<=2%), while running 5-10x faster and ~10x cheaper. On jailbreak detection, the tradeoff shifts: frontier LLMs achieve higher detection and lower false-positive rates but at 10-50x higher cost and 5-10x higher latency. We release the benchmark, framework, leaderboard, and datasets as the first vendor-neutral basis for selecting safeguards under real deployment constraints.
tldr: This paper benchmarks LLM supervision systems for content moderation and jailbreak detection, focusing on operational trade-offs like cost and latency.
motivation: Existing benchmarks for LLM supervision systems are vendor-biased and ignore cost and latency, which are critical for real deployment.
method: The authors evaluate 28 systems from 17 providers on detection rate, false-positive rate, latency, and cost using in-house datasets with paraphrased synthetic samples.
result: Specialized guardrails match frontier LLMs on content moderation but are faster and cheaper; for jailbreak detection, frontier LLMs perform better but at higher cost and latency.
conclusion: The choice of supervision system depends on use-case-specific trade-offs, and the benchmark provides a vendor-neutral basis for selection.

title: Amplify, Don't Create: Temporal Accumulation For Slow-Burn Prompt Injection
authors: J Alex Corll
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20746v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Most prompt-injection detectors score a single event or message. Control-plane attacks against tool-using agents can instead distribute weak directives across a trajectory while keeping each event below threshold. We test whether a proxy-side temporal accumulator recovers this slow-burn signal by reducing frozen per-event scores to peak and CUSUM persistence statistics. To avoid circularity, grafts are generated against a held-out autoregressive cloaking target and then re-scored under a detector of record: a frozen char-ngram SVM plus an embedding-contrastive head. Only floor-met grafts bound to executed action edges and still sub-threshold under the detector of record enter the slow-burn endpoint. This is a boundary result, not a deployable detector. On concentrated attacks, trajectory-level accumulation beats the per-event foil under a clustered bootstrap (gap +0.092, 95% CI [+0.025, +0.155]), while persistence and peak are statistically tied. On git repo-exfil, density-four floor-met sub-threshold grafts add persistence mass that matched benign shams do not (persistence-delta AUC 0.708 over four attack survivors and six benign shams), while the matched peak-delta control does not separate attack from sham (AUC 0.417), localizing the effect to accumulated persistence rather than a single hot graft. The effect fails on broader clean-path actions (persistence-delta AUC 0.167), where the detector assigns attack and benign actions indistinguishable per-event scores, leaving no margin for CUSUM to bank. Independent powering is blocked by only three to four independent tasks. Temporal accumulation is therefore a narrow-band margin amplifier: it can bank elevated sub-threshold signal but cannot create margin where the per-event detector has none. As byproducts, we contribute a pseudo-replication warning and an independence-audit standard for agent-benchmark evaluation.
tldr: This paper proposes a temporal accumulation method to detect slow-burn prompt injection attacks in tool-using agents, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Prompt injection attacks can be distributed across multiple events to evade per-event detectors; the authors aim to recover this slow-burn signal using temporal accumulation.
method: They use a frozen char-ngram SVM plus embedding-contrastive head as detector, and apply peak and CUSUM persistence statistics to accumulate per-event scores over a trajectory.
result: Temporal accumulation beats per-event detection on concentrated attacks (gap +0.092) and separates attack from benign on repo-exfil (persistence-delta AUC 0.708), but fails when per-event scores are indistinguishable.
conclusion: Temporal accumulation is a narrow-band margin amplifier that can bank elevated sub-threshold signal but cannot create margin where the per-event detector has none.

title: Synthetic Network Packet Generation Through Statistical Learning And Genetic Algorithms
authors: Mayank Raj, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Lance Fiondella, Gokhan Kul
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Developing robust intrusion detection systems (IDS) for IoT environments requires large, labeled datasets capturing realistic traffic distributions across both benign and malicious activity. Existing public datasets suffer from fixed activity distributions and extreme class imbalance, while deep generative models (GANs, VAEs) provide no mechanism to enforce that synthetic packets remain within physically valid feature ranges. This paper proposes and compares two constraint-enforcing approaches for synthetic IoT network packet generation: (i) a statistical learning method combining PCA-based latent space sampling with dual One-Class SVM (OCSVM) and Isolation Forest (IF) boundary enforcement, and (ii) a genetic algorithm (GA) method that treats packet generation as a multi-objective optimization problem with explicit fitness criteria for anomaly model acceptance and distributional fidelity. Both methods embed hard validity constraints -- dual anomaly-detection gating, feature-range clamping, and independent validation -- directly into the synthesis pipeline. Evaluation on the complete ACI IoT 2023 dataset (1,231,411 packets, 12 attack categories, class imbalance up to 175,805:1) demonstrates that both methods achieve PASS status across all categories under independently trained validators with a 30% anomaly rate threshold: the statistical method attains 1.20% average anomaly rate with ~1,091 packets/s throughput, while the GA attains 0.62% average anomaly rate with organic per-class variance (0.00%-2.50%) at ~5.7 packets/s. Both methods successfully amplify the 5-sample ARP Spoofing category by 200x to 1,000 validated packets. The ~190:1 throughput ratio between methods, combined with their complementary quality profiles, provides evidence-based selection criteria for deployment contexts ranging from rapid dataset augmentation to adversarial robustness testing.
tldr: This paper proposes statistical learning and genetic algorithm methods for synthetic network packet generation to improve intrusion detection systems, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Existing IoT network datasets suffer from class imbalance and lack of realistic traffic distributions, hindering IDS development.
method: Two constraint-enforcing approaches are compared: a statistical method using PCA and anomaly detection (OCSVM, Isolation Forest), and a genetic algorithm treating packet generation as multi-objective optimization.
result: Both methods achieve low anomaly rates (1.20% and 0.62%) and can amplify rare attack categories, with the statistical method being much faster.
conclusion: The methods provide complementary trade-offs between speed and quality, useful for dataset augmentation and adversarial robustness testing.

title: Can LLMs Reason About Brand Ownership? An Empirical Study Of Domain Attribution Intelligence
authors: Mohamed Nabeel Fathima Mashood
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a new domain resembling a popular brand appears, defenders face a fundamental ambiguity: it may be an attacker-created squatting site for phishing, or it may be a domain the brand itself registered, either defensively, to block attackers, or legitimately, for a new product or service launch. Incorrectly flagging a brand-owned domain as malicious produces a false positive that harms end users and damages the brand's reputation. Resolving this ambiguity requires brand intelligence: the ability to determine, at scale, whether a given domain belongs to a brand. Large language models (LLMs), with their broad knowledge of brand domain relationships, offer a promising zero configuration approach to this problem, but their reliability for brand intelligence tasks remains unknown. We present the first systematic empirical evaluation of LLM brand intelligence across three tasks: domain enumeration (Q1), open ended brand attribution (Q2), and binary ownership classification (Q3). We evaluate four models, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and Claude Sonnet 4.6, across four retrieval settings (in context, web search, WHOIS lookup, and combined) on 36 of the most phished brands. Our results reveal a stark dichotomy: models achieve up to 82% precision enumerating brand domains from memory alone, yet fail at ownership verification without external tools, with macro F1 at most 0.37 in ICL mode. WHOIS augmentation lifts Q3 macro F1 by up to 0.65 points, yielding near perfect precision (<= 0.99), dramatically reducing the false positive risk for defenders. We provide concrete recommendations for deploying LLMs in brand protection pipelines.
tldr: This paper evaluates LLMs' ability to determine whether a domain belongs to a brand, focusing on cybersecurity applications.
motivation: Defenders need to distinguish between brand-owned domains and attacker-created squatting sites to avoid false positives in phishing detection.
method: The authors test four LLMs on three tasks (domain enumeration, open-ended attribution, binary ownership classification) with different retrieval settings (in-context, web search, WHOIS, combined) across 36 phished brands.
result: LLMs achieve up to 82% precision in enumerating brand domains from memory but fail at ownership verification without external tools; WHOIS augmentation improves macro F1 by up to 0.65 points.
conclusion: LLMs are not reliable for brand ownership verification without external data sources, but can be useful in brand protection pipelines with proper augmentation.

title: Whose Agent Are You? Multi-Layer Fingerprinting And Attribution Of Autonomous Web Agents
authors: Dayeon Kang, Hyejun Jeong, Jade Sheffey, Pubali Datta, Amir Houmansadr
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As AI web agents proliferate, combining large language models with autonomous, browser-level control, indiscriminate content scraping by web agents has emerged as a privacy and security challenge. Existing defenses, such as robots.txt and active bot-blocking, are insufficient, as they are widely violated and easily circumvented. In this work, we demonstrate that AI web agents can be effectively distinguished from humans and traditional crawlers using a multi-layer fingerprint based on both network layer characteristics (e.g., TLS, HTTP) and browser interaction behavior. We implement this mechanism as a programmatic logging framework that can be deployed on a live, instrumented domain. By analyzing six prominent agent frameworks (AutoGen, Browser Use, Claude, Gemini, Operator, and Skyvern), we uncover latent structural differences in how these systems assemble HTTP requests, establish TLS/HTTP connections, and execute autonomous browser actions. Feeding these multi-layer features into a decision tree classifier, our framework achieves high-fidelity identification (97% accuracy), successfully isolating distinct agent architectures and differentiating agent traffic from both human browsing baselines and legacy crawlers. Our findings demonstrate that cross-layer agent tracking provides a robust, evasion-resistant strategy for content protection and web security policy enforcement.
tldr: This paper proposes a multi-layer fingerprinting method to distinguish AI web agents from humans and traditional crawlers for content protection.
motivation: Existing defenses like robots.txt and bot-blocking are insufficient against AI web agents that scrape content indiscriminately.
method: The authors develop a logging framework that captures network-layer (TLS, HTTP) and browser interaction features, then use a decision tree classifier to identify agent frameworks.
result: The classifier achieves 97% accuracy in distinguishing six agent frameworks from human browsing and legacy crawlers.
conclusion: Cross-layer agent tracking provides a robust, evasion-resistant strategy for web security policy enforcement.

title: Think Twice Before You Act: Protecting Llm Agents Against Tool Description Poisoning Via Isolated Planning
authors: Shanghao Shi, Xiao Wang, Chaoyu Zhang, Hao Li, Wenjing Lou, Thomas Hou, Yevgeniy Vorobeychik, Chongjie Zhang, Ning Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The integration of external tools has substantially expanded the capabilities of large language model (LLM) agents, but it also introduces new attack surfaces beyond prompt injection. In particular, cross-tool description poisoning can manipulate planner-visible tool metadata to steer an agent's trajectory, even if the poisoned tool itself is never chosen. To understand the effectiveness of existing defenses against this emerging threat, we first evaluate several prompt-injection defenses and find that they transfer poorly to cross-tool description poisoning. A key observation is that poisoned descriptions persist in the planning context across steps, enabling continuous influence over subsequent tool choices. Building on this insight, we propose Tool-Guard, a novel system-level defense based on a new concept called isolated planning, in which tool invocations that are detected as misaligned or suspicious cause the corresponding tool to be placed in a quarantined list (the influenced list), breaking further influence from poisoned descriptions. With this influence isolated, the tool can continue to be used to support the task, enabling a robust defense that preserves legitimate tool utility. Experiments on the AgentDojo and ASB benchmarks show that Tool-Guard substantially reduces attack success while maintaining high task utility. Our code is available at [URL].
tldr: This paper proposes a defense against tool description poisoning attacks on LLM agents, using isolated planning to quarantine suspicious tool descriptions.
motivation: LLM agents that use external tools are vulnerable to cross-tool description poisoning, where poisoned tool metadata can steer the agent's trajectory even if the poisoned tool is never invoked.
method: The authors propose Tool-Guard, a system-level defense that detects misaligned or suspicious tool invocations and places the corresponding tool in a quarantined list, breaking further influence from poisoned descriptions while allowing legitimate use.
result: Experiments on AgentDojo and ASB benchmarks show that Tool-Guard substantially reduces attack success while maintaining high task utility.
conclusion: Isolated planning is an effective defense against cross-tool description poisoning, preserving tool utility while mitigating attacks.

title: Equilibrium With Internal Transfers
authors: Mingyang Liu, Gabriele Farina, Asuman Ozdaglar
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20960v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nash equilibrium (NE) arises from selfish utility maximization, yet its social welfare can be arbitrarily far from optimal. Moreover, computing an NE is intractable in general. We study augmented game models in which players use budget-balanced internal transfers to improve incentives before play. We first introduce (SETE), where players commit to nonnegative peer-to-peer transfers that are paid only if the recipient does not deviate from a prescribed strategy. For polymatrix games, we show that every stationary point of the social welfare function, in particular any socially optimal strategy profile, can be sustained as a SETE. This induces a Nash equilibrium in the agent normal form of the corresponding augmented game. We further propose a polynomial-time algorithm and a decentralized learning dynamic to compute such product-form equilibria. We then introduce (M-SETE), where a mediator makes both the payment schedule and the prescribed strategies binding offers. This additional enforcement resolves the agent-normal-form limitation: an M-SETE is a Nash equilibrium of the augmented game itself, not merely of its agent normal form, and any socially optimal strategy profile can be supported as an M-SETE in any finite game while preserving budget balance. Thus, internal transfers improve welfare and computation while preserving independent play on the equilibrium path. When full sequential-game stability is required, binding mediation provides the corresponding implementation.
tldr: The paper introduces game-theoretic models with internal transfers to achieve socially optimal Nash equilibria in polymatrix and finite games.
motivation: Nash equilibria can be socially inefficient and hard to compute; the authors aim to design mechanisms that improve welfare and tractability via budget-balanced internal transfers.
method: They propose two equilibrium concepts: SETE (with peer-to-peer transfers) and M-SETE (with a mediator), and provide polynomial-time algorithms and decentralized learning dynamics.
result: Any socially optimal strategy profile can be sustained as a SETE in polymatrix games and as an M-SETE in any finite game, while preserving budget balance.
conclusion: Internal transfers can align individual incentives with social welfare and simplify computation, with binding mediation ensuring stability in sequential games.

title: Text-to-Image Generative Ai For Modeling And Simulation: Methods, Opportunities, And Applications
authors: Philippe J. Giabbanelli
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20991v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Text-to-image generation is a form of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) that converts textual descriptions into images. Most applications of GenAI in modeling and simulation (M&S) have focused on large language models for documentation, coding, or explanation. By contrast, the potential of image generation remains largely unexplored. This tutorial introduces text-to-image generation to the M&S community and details how it can support several M&S tasks, including communicating conceptual models, visualizing simulation outcomes, generating educational materials, and interfacing heterogeneous models in multi-scale simulations. The tutorial combines conceptual guidance with practical workflows, explaining how modern image generators operate, how prompts and simulation outputs can be translated into visual scenes, and how practitioners can integrate these tools into reproducible local pipelines. By focusing on transferable principles rather than specific tools, the tutorial equips M&S practitioners with the knowledge needed to evaluate, adopt, and adapt text-to-image generation in their simulation workflows.
tldr: A tutorial on using text-to-image generative AI for modeling and simulation tasks.
motivation: To introduce the M&S community to the potential of text-to-image generation, which is underexplored compared to LLMs.
method: Conceptual guidance and practical workflows for integrating text-to-image generators into simulation pipelines.
result: Demonstrates applications in communicating conceptual models, visualizing outcomes, generating educational materials, and interfacing heterogeneous models.
conclusion: Text-to-image generation can enhance M&S workflows, and practitioners can adopt these tools via reproducible local pipelines.

title: Do Large Language Model Voters Strategize? An Oracle-Based Benchmark For Manipulation Under Voting Rules
authors: Seyed Pouyan Mousavi Davoudi, Alireza Amiri-Margavi, Amin Gholami Davodi, Hamidreza Hasani Balyani, Arshia Gharagozlou
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21001v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strategic voting is a canonical failure mode for collective choice: a voter may obtain a more preferred outcome by reporting a ballot that differs from its true preferences. This paper introduces an oracle-based benchmark for testing whether large language model (LLM) voters can discover and execute such manipulations. Each instance gives an LLM voter a true preference ranking, the other voters' ballots, a deterministic voting rule, and a prompt condition. An exact oracle enumerates every feasible report by the LLM voter, computes the sincere outcome, identifies all profitable reports, and records the best achievable outcome. The benchmark therefore supplies ground truth for strategic success without human labels or subjective grading of explanations. The benchmark covers plurality, Borda, approval, instant-runoff voting, and Copeland-style pairwise majority voting; prompt conditions separate sincere, strategic, civic, and expert framings. To keep the primary study defensible while preserving the main comparisons, the registered core design fixes a single electorate size, uses 600 balanced election instances, and produces 9,600 model--prompt responses when run with four model configurations and four prompt conditions. Because existing peer-reviewed work does not report manipulation discovery, optimal manipulation, false manipulation, near-miss, or invalid-ballot rates for this exact task, we do not impute LLM performance from unrelated studies. Instead, we report exact oracle-calibration baselines that bound and contextualize subsequent model results. By reducing strategic-voting behavior to exact counterfactual evaluation, the benchmark turns the question ``Do LLM voters vote sincerely or strategically?'' into a reproducible social-choice experiment.
tldr: This paper introduces an oracle-based benchmark to test whether LLMs can engage in strategic voting under various voting rules.
motivation: Strategic voting is a known failure mode in collective choice, and the authors aim to evaluate if LLMs can discover and execute such manipulations.
method: The benchmark uses an exact oracle to enumerate all feasible reports, compute sincere outcomes, and identify profitable manipulations for LLM voters across multiple voting rules and prompt conditions.
result: The benchmark provides ground truth for strategic success without human labels, covering plurality, Borda, approval, instant-runoff, and Copeland voting.
conclusion: The benchmark enables reproducible experiments on whether LLMs vote sincerely or strategically, reducing the question to exact counterfactual evaluation.

title: Quantifying The Impact Of Stealthy Ble Spam & Flooding Attacks On IoT Environments
authors: Usman Rauf, Adalynn Martinez, Fadi Mohsen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The energy-efficient design of the BLE protocol, emphasis on rapid, and userfriendly discovery, making it an ideal choice for IoMTs, specifically, military field medical systems, and battlefield wearable sensors. Especially in active conflict zones, when static medical facilities are vulnerable and often targeted, limiting their viability for sustained care delivery. This rapid deployment, and ease of management comes at the cost of expanded attack surface, i.e., BLE flooding attacks. During such attacks, adversaries flood advertisement channels with unauthorized connection or advertising requests to exhaust nearby device resources and disrupt legitimate communication, sometimes culminating in denial-of-service conditions. A first public proof-of-concept of such attacks, using a Raspberry Pi has since been adapted to commodity platforms (e.g., Flipper Zero, HackRF, Android), lowering the barrier to attack. In contested environments, such platforms are directly relevant to adversarial RF jamming and spoofing operations, where low-cost, portable devices can induce disproportionate disruption in dense wireless ecosystems. In this work, we develop a quantitative foundation for understanding the impact of such attacks and propose a practical deterrence strategy based on agility to raise the cost of such attacks.
tldr: This paper analyzes BLE flooding and spam attacks on IoT environments and proposes a deterrence strategy based on agility.
motivation: BLE's energy-efficient design makes it ideal for IoMTs but also vulnerable to flooding attacks that can disrupt communication in contested environments.
method: The authors develop a quantitative foundation for understanding attack impact and propose a practical deterrence strategy using agility to raise attack costs.
result: The paper provides a quantitative analysis of BLE flooding attacks and demonstrates a deterrence approach.
conclusion: The proposed agility-based strategy can mitigate BLE flooding attacks, but the work is focused on cybersecurity, not quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Honeyquest For LLMs: Rethinking Cyber Deception For Ai Attackers
authors: Kerri Prinos, Lilianne Brush, Cameron Denton
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21037v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The empirical foundation of cyber deception relies on human-centered hypotheses, but the rapid emergence of autonomous, AI-enabled attackers challenges whether this foundation transfers to AI agents. To address this, we introduce an automated evaluation framework adapted from the Honeyquest instrument to assess LLM attacker judgment at scale. Our 21-LLM cohort spanned 10 providers, diverse architectures and specializations, open- and closed-weight models, and parameter scales from 8B to over 1T. We evaluated the performance of this LLM cohort (yielding 10,962 responses) against the 47-participant human baseline across an identical set of 174 reconnaissance queries. Our empirical evaluation reveals three key findings that establish LLMs as a distinct attacker class: (1) every model in our cohort falls for deceptive traps at a significantly higher rate than human attackers; (2) the defensive attention-diversion effect observed in humans is statistically absent in our LLM cohort; and (3) a critical recognition-action gap, where LLMs successfully articulate trap recognition in their reasoning but exploit the deceptive elements anyway 73.4\% of the time. Across the 21 models, trap recognition in reasoning text did not predict fell-for-trap behavior (Spearman [MATH], [MATH]). Ultimately, these findings demonstrate that human-centered deception hypotheses do not reliably transfer to AI attackers, highlighting the critical need for new research into AI-native active defense frameworks.
tldr: This paper evaluates LLM attackers' susceptibility to cyber deception, finding that human-centered deception hypotheses do not transfer to AI agents.
motivation: The rise of autonomous AI attackers challenges the human-centered foundation of cyber deception, necessitating an evaluation of whether existing deception strategies work against LLMs.
method: The authors adapt the Honeyquest framework to test 21 LLMs (10,962 responses) against a human baseline (47 participants) on 174 reconnaissance queries, measuring trap-falling rates and reasoning.
result: LLMs fall for traps at significantly higher rates than humans, lack the defensive attention-diversion effect, and exhibit a recognition-action gap where they recognize traps but exploit them 73.4% of the time.
conclusion: Human-centered deception hypotheses do not reliably transfer to AI attackers, highlighting the need for AI-native active defense frameworks.

title: Ovig: Optimistic Verification Of Ai Training Integrity Via Gradient Signals
authors: Hongxu Su, Jianzhu Yao, Huan Zhang, Xuechao Wang, Pramod Viswanath
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid growth of AI has increased the demand for domain-specific post-training, while the cost and specialization of accelerator infrastructure push many model owners to outsource this process.
